problem_statement.title: MarkdownHeaderSplitter treats headings inside longer closing fences as headers
problem_statement.body:
## Problem

`MarkdownHeaderSplitter` excludes headers inside fenced code blocks only if the closing fence has exactly the same length as the opening fence. Markdown permits a closing fence of the same type with *at least* as many fence characters. With a longer valid closing fence, the splitter treats code comments as document headers and cuts the code block apart.

## Reproduction

On current `main`:

```python
from haystack import Document
from haystack.components.preprocessors import MarkdownHeaderSplitter

text = "# Intro\nBody\n````python\n# fake\n`````\n## Real\nEnd\n"
result = MarkdownHeaderSplitter().run(documents=[Document(content=text)])
print([doc.meta["header"] for doc in result["documents"]])
```

Actual: `['Intro', 'fake', 'Real']`. Expected: `['Intro', 'Real']`. I ran it twice with identical results. Replacing the five-backtick closer with a four-backtick closer gives the expected result. The same failure occurs with four opening tildes and five closing tildes.

The current `_code_block_pattern` uses a backreference to the opening fence, requiring equal lengths. The CommonMark rule is a closing fence of the same type with *at least* the opening length: https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#fenced-code-blocks .

## Suggested scope

Recognize longer closing fences when excluding code blocks from header matches, while keeping unrelated heading and secondary-split behavior unchanged. Regression tests should cover longer backtick and tilde closers, equal-length closers, and the real header after the block. This should not require a public API change. I did not find a matching open/closed issue or PR and can prepare a patch once the current Haystack PR queue clears.

title: Fix Coulomb friction limits in penalty solvers
issue_title: [BUG] SemiImplicit/Featherstone rigid friction exceeds Coulomb limit (Huber-normalized direction)

gold_patch:
diff --git a/changelog/4796.deprecated.md b/changelog/4796.deprecated.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..c9eb305e4d7
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Deprecate the `friction_smoothing` argument and attribute of `SolverSemiImplicit` and `SolverFeatherstone`; constructor calls and attribute access remain supported, but the value no longer affects friction. Explicit constructor values and attribute reads or assignments emit a deprecation warning. Remove its use and configure shape material `kf` for the low-speed friction slope and `mu` for the Coulomb limit.
diff --git a/changelog/4796.fixed.md b/changelog/4796.fixed.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..1f4385f81d0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog/4796.fixed.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Enforce the Coulomb friction limit in `SolverSemiImplicit` and `SolverFeatherstone`, including normal damping, and preserve the viscous velocity gradient at zero slip. Sliding friction may be substantially lower than with the previous Huber-normalized calculation.
diff --git a/docs/concepts/collisions.rst b/docs/concepts/collisions.rst
index 32fffb844e8..4f8c00e82b3 100644
--- a/docs/concepts/collisions.rst
+++ b/docs/concepts/collisions.rst
@@ -2326,15 +2326,28 @@ normal and tangential relative velocities. Per contact, the normal force
 
    f_n &= k_e \, d \qquad (d < k_a) \\
    f_d &= k_d \, \min(v_n, 0) \qquad (d < 0) \\
-   \lVert f_t \rVert &= k_f \, \lVert v_t \rVert \qquad (d < 0, \text{ low slip speed})
+   \lVert f_t \rVert &= \min(k_f \, \lVert v_t \rVert,\, \mu |f_n + f_d|) \qquad (d < 0)
 
 **Friction gain** ``kf`` **[N·s/m]** is the slope of a viscous regularization
 of Coulomb friction: at low slip speed the friction force is
 :math:`k_f \lVert v_t \rVert`, so a body at rest on a slope creeps instead of
 sticking. With :math:`N` contacts carrying the load, the creep speed is roughly
-:math:`m g \sin\theta / (N k_f)`. At higher slip speed the force is capped by a
-term proportional to ``mu``. The exact cap is under review in
-`#4796 <https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/issues/4796>`__.
+:math:`m g \sin\theta / (N k_f)`. At higher slip speed the force is capped at
+:math:`\mu |f_n + f_d|`, including normal damping. Friction opposes tangential
+relative motion. For positive ``kf``, the transition speed is
+:math:`\mu |f_n + f_d| / k_f`.
+
+The viscous branch evaluates :math:`k_f v_t` directly, so its velocity
+derivative remains well-defined at rest without a separate smoothing
+parameter. The force is continuous at the Coulomb limit, where its derivative
+changes between the viscous and capped branches.
+
+The solver argument and attribute ``friction_smoothing`` are deprecated in
+Newton 1.8 and have no effect on friction. Explicit constructor values and
+attribute reads or assignments emit a deprecation warning. Constructor calls
+and attribute access remain supported, and the attribute retains its last

problem_statement.title: [BUG] SemiImplicit/Featherstone rigid friction exceeds Coulomb limit (Huber-normalized direction)
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

In `SolverSemiImplicit` and `SolverFeatherstone`, rigid contact friction can exceed the Coulomb limit `mu * |f_n|` by a large factor at ordinary sliding speeds.

`_eval_body_contact` in `newton/_src/solvers/semi_implicit/kernels_contact.py` (used by both solvers) computes:

```python
vs = wp.norm_huber(vt, delta=friction_smoothing)
if vs > 0.0:
    fr = vt / vs
    ft = fr * wp.min(kf * vs, -mu * (fn + fd))
```

`fr` is meant to be the slip direction, but `vt / vs` is not a unit vector, because `norm_huber` is `0.5 * |v|^2` for `|v| <= delta` and `delta * (|v| - delta / 2)` above it. The viscous branch is unaffected (`|ft| = kf * |vt|`), but in the capped branch:

- `|vt| <= delta`: `|ft| = 2 * mu * |fn + fd| / |vt|`, which is above Coulomb for any `|vt| < 2` m/s at the default `delta = 1`.
- `|vt| > delta`: `|ft| = mu * |fn + fd| * |vt| / (delta * (|vt| - delta / 2))`, which goes to `mu * |fn + fd| / delta` at high speed. A smaller `friction_smoothing` therefore makes friction stronger, not just sharper.

Per contact, the peak friction is about `sqrt(2 * kf * mu * |fn + fd|)`. For an 8 kg box on 4 contacts with the default `kf = 1000` and `mu = 0.5`, that is about 14x the Coulomb limit.

The script below slides a box at 0.5 m/s with `mu = 0.5`. The expected Coulomb deceleration is `mu * g ≈ 4.9` m/s², and the measured value is about 19.5 m/s². With `friction_smoothing=0.1`, a box sliding at 5 m/s decelerates at roughly 150 m/s² and tips over.

Expected behavior: `|ft| = min(kf * |vt|, mu * |fn + fd|)`, i.e. the direction normalized by `|vt|`, with the Huber smoothing affecting only the behavior near `|vt| = 0`. This should be fixed without regressing the gradient stability that motivated the Huber norm.

This also blocks documenting `kf` accurately (#4727).

### Reproduction Script

```python
import warp as wp

import newton

MU, V0, DT = 0.5, 0.5, 1e-4

builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
builder.default_shape_cfg.mu = MU
builder.default_shape_cfg.ke = 1e5
builder.default_shape_cfg.kd = 1e3
builder.add_ground_plane()
body = builder.add_body(xform=wp.transform((0.0, 0.0, 0.1), wp.quat_identity()))
builder.add_shape_box(body, hx=0.1, hy=0.1, hz=0.1)
model = builder.finalize()

solver = newton.solvers.SolverSemiImplicit(model)  # friction_smoothing=1.0
pipeline = newton.CollisionPipeline(model)
contacts = pipeline.contacts()
s0, s1, control = model.state(), model.state(), model.control()


def step():
    global s0, s1
    s0.clear_forces()
    pipeline.collide(s0, contacts)
    solver.step(s0, s1, control, contacts, DT)
    s0, s1 = s1, s0


for _ in range(3000):  # settle on the ground
    step()

qd = s0.body_qd.numpy()
qd[0, 0] = V0
s0.body_qd.assign(qd)

n = 200
for _ in range(n):
    step()

decel = (V0 - s0.body_qd.numpy()[0, 0]) / (n * DT)
print(f"deceleration {decel:.2f} m/s^2, Coulomb mu*g = {MU * 9.81:.2f} m/s^2")
# deceleration 19.49 m/s^2, Coulomb mu*g = 4.91 m/s^2
```

- Newton: main (756912b1f)
- Warp: 1.18.0
- Python: 3.12.3
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- GPU: NVIDIA L4

gold_patch:
diff --git a/ninja/schema.py b/ninja/schema.py
index c5f477b2b..df55687ad 100644
--- a/ninja/schema.py
+++ b/ninja/schema.py
@@ -76,9 +76,20 @@ def __getattr__(self, key: str) -> Any:
                 except AttributeError:
                     try:
                         # value = attrgetter(key)(self._obj)
-                        value = Variable(key).resolve(self._obj)
+                        variable = Variable(key)
                         # TODO: Variable(key) __init__ is actually slower than
                         #       Variable.resolve - so it better be cached
+                        if variable.lookups is None:
+                            # Variable comes from the template language, so
+                            # it parses constants as well as lookups: "0" and
+                            # "1.5" are numbers, "'x'" is a string. These have
+                            # no lookups, and resolve() returns the constant
+                            # without touching the object. A field with
+                            # alias="0" would then be "found" with the value 0.
+                            # Report it as missing instead, so that pydantic
+                            # tries the field name or uses the default.
+                            raise AttributeError(key)
+                        value = variable.resolve(self._obj)
                     except VariableDoesNotExist as e:
                         raise AttributeError(key) from e
         return self._convert_result(value)

problem_statement.title: prefect_docker: Default volumes not mounted when running docker flows directly
problem_statement.body:
### Bug summary

When running [flows directly in dynamic infrastructure](https://docs.prefect.io/v3/deploy/submit-flows-directly-to-dynamic-infrastructure), I believe there is a bug when spinning up new docker images when no storage is configured for the docker work pool. Let's say you create a docker work-pool 'docker' and set volumes to `["result-storage:/result-storage"]`. This volume is not mounted in the flow container. Using `docker inspect {imageTag}` on the image created by the worker, I can see that:
```json
"Volumes": {
                "/tmp/": {}
            }
```

I think the issue is in the file `prefect_docker/worker.py`. Specifically [here](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d4d41615e614b9f46eb317a2948a3d0643a07f5/src/integrations/prefect-docker/prefect_docker/worker.py#L507). The problem seems to be with the path `configuration.properties.volumes.default`. In the docker base job template, the default volumes are stored under the key `variables.properties.volumes.default`...

problem_statement.title: ORPO/CPO: a prompt that fills `max_length` gives an empty completion and NaN weights
problem_statement.body:
When the tokenized prompt alone reaches `max_length`, `ORPOTrainer` and `CPOTrainer` keep the whole prompt and truncate the completion to 0 tokens ([orpo_trainer.py#L532-L544](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/643ab11435db2080ccd694cbc4fb0b490a38d8ef/trl/experimental/orpo/orpo_trainer.py#L532-L544), [cpo_trainer.py#L550-L562](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/643ab11435db2080ccd694cbc4fb0b490a38d8ef/trl/experimental/cpo/cpo_trainer.py#L550-L562)). The row is kept, longer than `max_length`, with no completion token. The averaged log-prob then divides 0 by 0 ([orpo_trainer.py#L741](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/643ab11435db2080ccd694cbc4fb0b490a38d8ef/trl/experimental/orpo/orpo_trainer.py#L741), [cpo_trainer.py#L788](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/643ab11435db2080ccd694cbc4fb0b490a38d8ef/trl/experimental/cpo/cpo_trainer.py#L788)), so the gradient is NaN and the optimizer step writes NaN into every parameter. ORPO always averages; CPO averages for `simpo` and `ipo`. CPO `sigmoid` sums instead and silently scores the empty completion as log-prob 0.

#6548 planned two fixes: truncate each completion on its own budget, and drop the rows the prompt fills, like DPO and SFT do. #6588 shipped the first and a warning, not the drop.

### Reproduction

```python
from datasets import Dataset
from trl.experimental.cpo import CPOConfig, CPOTrainer
from trl.experimental.orpo import ORPOConfig, ORPOTrainer

dataset = Dataset.from_dict(
    {
        "prompt": ["The sky is", "Tell me a long story about " + "a very old lighthouse keeper and the sea, " * 4],
        "chosen": [" blue.", " Once upon a time there was a keeper."],
        "rejected": [" green.", " No."],
    }
)

for name, config_cls, trainer_cls, extra in [
    ("ORPO", ORPOConfig, ORPOTrainer, {}),
    ("CPO sigmoid", CPOConfig, CPOTrainer, {"loss_type": "sigmoid"}),
    ("CPO simpo", CPOConfig, CPOTrainer, {"loss_type": "simpo", "cpo_alpha": 0.0}),
]:
    args = config_cls(
        output_dir="out", max_length=32, per_device_train_batch_size=2, max_steps=1, logging_steps=1, report_to="none", **extra
    )
    trainer = trainer_cls(
        model="trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2ForCausalLM-2.5", args=args, train_dataset=dataset
    )
    row = trainer.train_dataset[1]
    print(f"{name}: max_length=32, long row: prompt={len(row['prompt_input_ids'])} tokens, chosen row={len(row['chosen_input_ids'])} tokens, chosen labels != -100: {sum(l != -100 for l in row['chosen_labels'])}")
    trainer.train()
    log = trainer.state.log_history[0]
    nan_params = sum(p.isnan().any().item() for p in trainer.model.parameters())
    print(f"{name}: loss={log['loss']} logps/chosen={log.get('logps/chosen')} grad_norm={log.get('grad_norm')} params with NaN after the step: {nan_params}")
```

outputs:

```
[RANK 0] The prompt alone fills `max_length`, so truncation leaves an empty completion. Consider increasing `max_length` or filtering out long prompts.
ORPO: max_length=32, long row: prompt=47 tokens, chosen row=47 tokens, chosen labels != -100: 0
ORPO: loss=0.0 logps/chosen=nan grad_norm=nan params with NaN after the step: 27
CPO sigmoid: max_length=32, long row: prompt=47 tokens, chosen row=47 tokens, chosen labels != -100: 0
CPO sigmoid: loss=12.620790481567383 logps/chosen=-17.891162872314453 grad_norm=1.765625 params with NaN after the step: 0
CPO simpo: max_length=32, long row: prompt=47 tokens, chosen row=47 tokens, chosen labels != -100: 0
CPO simpo: loss=0.0 logps/chosen=nan grad_norm=nan params with NaN after the step: 27
```

Expected: rows whose prompt fills `max_length` are dropped during preparation, as in DPO and SFT, so no row exceeds `max_length` and the loss stays finite.

### How did you hit this?

Found while auditing the TRL patches in Unsloth (unslothai/unsloth at ddb9065, unslothai/unsloth-zoo at d139fd2), then reproduced on TRL `main` with the script above. Unsloth truncates the prompt itself in ORPO/CPO `tokenize_row` ([rl_replacements.py#L1455-L1495](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/blob/ddb906524a85e715056205ab9b6c1e13687d19ab/unsloth/models/rl_replacements.py#L1455-L1495), unslothai/unsloth#12115). One long prompt in a batch is enough: all 27 parameter tensors of the model are NaN after the first step, and the logged loss reads 0.0.

problem_statement.title: [BUG] SuppressStdoutStderr in Prophet.fit() is not thread-safe and permanently redirects process FD 1/2 to /dev/null under concurrent execution
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

`Prophet` enables `suppress_stdout_stderror=True` by default (`darts/models/forecasting/prophet_model.py`), which wraps `self.model.fit(fit_df)` in `execute_and_suppress_output(..., logger, logging.WARNING, ...)` -> `SuppressStdoutStderr()` (`darts/logging.py`). Because `prophet_model.py` sets `logger.level = logging.WARNING` at import time, `SuppressStdoutStderr` is always entered by default.

`SuppressStdoutStderr` redirects OS-level file descriptors `1` (`stdout`) and `2` (`stderr`) process-wide using `os.dup` and `os.dup2` without any thread synchronization or reference counting:

```python
class SuppressStdoutStderr:
    def __init__(self):
        self.null_fds = [os.open(os.devnull, os.O_RDWR) for x in range(2)]
        self.save_fds = [os.dup(1), os.dup(2)]

    def __enter__(self):
        os.dup2(self.null_fds[0], 1)
        os.dup2(self.null_fds[1], 2)

    def __exit__(self, *_):
        os.dup2(self.save_fds[0], 1)
        os.dup2(self.save_fds[1], 2)
        for fd in self.null_fds + self.save_fds:
            os.close(fd)
```

This causes three problems:

1. **Permanent loss of `stdout` / `stderr` in multi-threaded execution (`ThreadPoolExecutor`)**:
   - Thread A enters `SuppressStdoutStderr`: `save_fds_A` duplicates the real FD 1/2, and `__enter__` points FD 1/2 to `os.devnull`.
   - While Thread A is inside `fit()`, Thread B instantiates `SuppressStdoutStderr`: `os.dup(1)` duplicates **the current FD 1 (which is `os.devnull`)** into `save_fds_B`.
   - Thread A finishes first and restores the real `stdout`/`stderr` to FD 1/2.
   - Thread B finishes second and executes `os.dup2(self.save_fds[0], 1)`, **permanently overwriting process FD 1 and FD 2 with `os.devnull` for the remainder of the Python process lifetime**.
2. **Crash in non-console environments (e.g., Windows GUI / `pythonw.exe` / background services)**:
   - When FD 1 or FD 2 is not associated with a valid OS file descriptor, `os.dup(1)` raises `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor`.
   - Additionally, because `os.open` and `os.dup` are called in `__init__` rather than `__enter__`, if the second `os.dup(2)` fails, the already-opened file descriptors in `self.null_fds` leak.
3. **Obsolescence with modern `prophet` (`cmdstanpy`)**:
   - `SuppressStdoutStderr` was originally needed when `fbprophet` used `pystan` (which wrote directly to C-level FD 1/2). Modern `prophet >= 1.1` uses `cmdstanpy`, which logs via standard Python `logging` (`logging.getLogger("cmdstanpy")` / `logging.getLogger("prophet")`).

---

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
import concurrent.futures
import time
from darts.logging import SuppressStdoutStderr


def worker(delay_enter: float, hold_time: float) -> None:
    time.sleep(delay_enter)
    with SuppressStdoutStderr():
        time.sleep(hold_time)


print("Before ThreadPoolExecutor (visible)")

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
    # Thread 1 enters at t=0.0s and exits at t=0.10s
    f1 = executor.submit(worker, 0.0, 0.10)
    # Thread 2 enters at t=0.02s (while FD 1/2 point to devnull) and exits at t=0.20s
    f2 = executor.submit(worker, 0.02, 0.20)
    f1.result()
    f2.result()

# Everything printed after this point is permanently lost to /dev/null!
print("After ThreadPoolExecutor (PERMANENTLY SILENCED - NEVER PRINTED!)")
```

Running this script prints `"Before ThreadPoolExecutor (visible)"` and never prints `"After ThreadPoolExecutor..."` because FD 1 and FD 2 remain pointing to `os.devnull`.

---

### Expected Behavior / Suggested Fix

1. If `SuppressStdoutStderr` is kept in `darts/logging.py`, it should be protected by a module-level lock + reference counter (so `save_fds` is only captured when the outermost context enters `refcount == 0 -> 1` and restored when the last context exits `refcount == 1 -> 0`), and all FD operations should happen inside `__enter__` with graceful fallback if `os.dup` raises `OSError`.
2. Alternatively, for `Prophet`, output suppression can be achieved thread-safely via `cmdstanpy` / `prophet` logger levels (or passing `show_console=False` / `refresh=0` to CmdStanPy) without mutating process-wide OS file descriptors.

---

### Environment

- Darts version: `0.48.1`

+# tests/test_mcp_http_call_timing.py
+"""Per-call timing lines and the timestamped MEMPALACE_LOG_FILE (#2620).
+
+Two guarantees are covered here:
+
+* every locked palace tool call emits exactly one
+  ``CALL <tool> <read|write> wait=<ms> run=<ms> <ok|error>`` line, with the
+  dispatch-lock wait measured separately from the handler run, and
+* the ``MEMPALACE_SLOW_CALL_WARN_SECS`` threshold escalates that line to a
+  WARNING ``SLOW CALL`` line when the call (either the queue wait or the
+  handler run) reaches it, while logging is never allowed to fail the call.
+
+The timing helper is driven directly rather than through a socket: the wait is
+only observable when the dispatch lock is already held by another thread, and
+that is exactly the queueing the issue is about.
+"""
+
+import logging
+import re
+import threading
+import time
+
+import pytest
+
+from mempalace import mcp_server as mcp
+
+_LOGGER_NAME = "mempalace.mcp_server"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def caplog_calls(caplog):
+    """Capture the MCP server logger at INFO for the duration of a test."""
+    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger=_LOGGER_NAME)
+    return caplog
+
+
+def _call_lines(caplog):
+    return [
+        r.getMessage().removeprefix("SLOW ")
+        for r in caplog.records
+        if r.getMessage().startswith("CALL ") or r.getMessage().startswith("SLOW CALL ")
+    ]
+
+
+_CALL_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^CALL (?P<tool>\S+) (?P<mode>read|write) "
+    r"wait=(?P<wait>\d+)ms run=(?P<run>\d+)ms (?P<out>ok|error)$"
+)
+
+
+class TestCallLineShape:
+    """One line per locked call, carrying tool, mode, wait, run and outcome."""
+
+    def test_read_call_emits_one_line_with_read_mode(self, caplog_calls):
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+            pass
+        lines = _call_lines(caplog_calls)
+        assert len(lines) == 1, lines
+        match = _CALL_RE.match(lines[0])
+        assert match, lines[0]
+        assert match["tool"] == "mempalace_search"
+        assert match["mode"] == "read"
+        assert match["out"] == "ok"
+        assert int(match["wait"]) >= 0 and int(match["run"]) >= 0
+
+    def test_write_call_reports_write_mode(self, caplog_calls):
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_diary_write", "write"):
+            pass
+        line = _call_lines(caplog_calls)[0]
+        assert _CALL_RE.match(line)["mode"] == "write"
+
+    def test_failing_call_is_logged_before_the_exception_propagates(self, caplog_calls):
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+            with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+        line = _call_lines(caplog_calls)[0]
+        assert _CALL_RE.match(line)["out"] == "error"
+
+    def test_lock_is_released_even_when_the_handler_raises(self):
+        """A failed call must not leak the dispatch lock to the next one."""
+        lock = mcp._RWLock()
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+            with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "write", (lock,)):
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+        assert not lock._writer and lock._readers == 0
+
+
+class TestWaitIsMeasuredApartFromRun:
+    """The line exists to separate a queued call from a slow one."""
+
+    def test_lock_contention_lands_in_wait_not_run(self, caplog_calls):
+        lock = mcp._RWLock()
+        held = threading.Event()
+        release = threading.Event()
+
+        def _holder():
+            with lock:
+                held.set()
+                release.wait(5)
+
+        holder = threading.Thread(target=_holder, daemon=True)
+        holder.start()
+        assert held.wait(5)
+        try:
+            with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read", (lock.read_lock(),)):
+                pass
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+            holder.join(timeout=5)
+
+        match = _CALL_RE.match(_call_lines(caplog_calls)[0])
+        # Only the wait can be long here: the handler body is empty.
+        assert int(match["wait"]) > 0, match.group(0)
+        assert int(match["run"]) == 0, match.group(0)
+
+    def test_slow_handler_lands_in_run_not_wait(self, caplog_calls):
+        lock = mcp._RWLock()
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read", (lock.read_lock(),)):
+            time.sleep(0.05)
+        match = _CALL_RE.match(_call_lines(caplog_calls)[0])
+        assert int(match["wait"]) == 0, match.group(0)
+        assert int(match["run"]) >= 40, match.group(0)
+
+
+class TestSlowCallEscalation:
+    """``MEMPALACE_SLOW_CALL_WARN_SECS`` escalates the line to WARNING."""
+
+    def test_default_threshold_is_20s(self):
+        assert mcp._http_slow_call_warn_secs() == mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_DEFAULT
+        assert mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_DEFAULT == 20.0
+
+    def test_fast_call_stays_at_info(self, caplog_calls):
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+            pass
+        record = next(r for r in caplog_calls.records if r.getMessage().startswith("CALL "))
+        assert record.levelno == logging.INFO
+
+    def test_slow_run_escalates_to_warning(self, caplog_calls, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv(mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_ENV, "0.05")
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+            time.sleep(0.08)
+        record = next(r for r in caplog_calls.records if r.getMessage().startswith("SLOW CALL "))
+        assert record.levelno == logging.WARNING
+        assert _CALL_RE.match(record.getMessage().removeprefix("SLOW "))
+
+    def test_zero_disables_the_escalation(self, caplog_calls, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv(mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_ENV, "0")
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+            time.sleep(0.08)
+        assert not any(r.getMessage().startswith("SLOW CALL ") for r in caplog_calls.records)
+
+    def test_malformed_value_warns_and_falls_back(self, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv(mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_ENV, "not-a-number")
+        assert mcp._http_slow_call_warn_secs() == mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_DEFAULT
+
+    def test_negative_value_is_clamped_to_disabled(self, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv(mcp._HTTP_SLOW_CALL_WARN_ENV, "-5")
+        assert mcp._http_slow_call_warn_secs() == 0.0
+
+
+class TestLoggingNeverFailsTheCall:
+    """A diagnostic must not be able to fail the tool call it describes."""
+
+    def test_logging_failure_does_not_propagate(self, monkeypatch, caplog_calls):
+        def _boom(*_args, **_kwargs):
+            raise RuntimeError("logging is broken")
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mcp.logger, "log", _boom)
+        with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+            pass  # must not raise
+
+    def test_logging_failure_does_not_swallow_a_handler_error(self, monkeypatch):
+        def _boom(*_args, **_kwargs):
+            raise RuntimeError("logging is broken")
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(mcp.logger, "log", _boom)
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="handler"):
+            with mcp._http_call_timing("mempalace_search", "read"):
+                raise ValueError("handler")
+
+
+class TestDispatchEmitsOneLinePerLockedCall:
+    """The lines come from ``_http_dispatch``, not only from direct use."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _tools_call(name):
+        return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": name}}

+        mcp._http_dispatch(self._tools_call("mempalace_search"))

+        monkeypatch.setattr(mcp, "handle_request", lambda _request: {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1})
+        mcp._http_dispatch(self._tools_call("mempalace_add_drawer"))
+        assert _CALL_RE.match(_call_lines(caplog_calls)[0])["mode"] == "write"

problem_statement.title: logging: MEMPALACE_LOG_FILE lines carry no timestamp - add one, and log one line per palace call with lock-wait and run time
problem_statement.body:
---

### Summary

The `MEMPALACE_LOG_FILE` handler formats bare `%(message)s` (`mempalace/mcp_server/_logging.py`, still so on `main` as of 2026-09-29), so a server-side log cannot be lined up against a client-side timeout. And there is no per-call record at all: `_http_dispatch` in `mempalace/mcp_server/http.py` takes the read or exclusive lock and calls `handle_request` with no timing, so the only timing signal is the write-stall watchdog. With the writer-preferring dispatch lock (#2398) a slow call and a call queued behind a writer look identical from the client - and from the log.

### Proposed change (we run it as a local patch and can send a PR)

- Formatter `"%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s"` on the `MEMPALACE_LOG_FILE` handler.
- In `_http_dispatch`, time the lock wait and the handler separately and log one INFO line per palace tool call: `CALL <tool> <read|write> wait=<ms> run=<ms> <ok|error>`; WARNING `SLOW CALL ...` at or above `MEMPALACE_SLOW_CALL_WARN_SECS` (default 20; parsed the same way as `MEMPALACE_MCP_WRITE_STALL_WARN_SECS`). Lock-free tools are unaffected. The logging call never raises, so a logging failure cannot fail the call.

### What it looks like on a live server (188k drawers, chromadb 1.5.9, two HTTP clients)

```
2026-09-15 09:49:06,548 WARNING SLOW CALL mempalace_status read wait=0ms run=36407ms ok
2026-09-15 09:59:43,301 INFO CALL mempalace_diary_read read wait=0ms run=31ms ok
2026-09-15 10:01:39,663 WARNING SLOW CALL mempalace_diary_write write wait=0ms run=78886ms ok
2026-09-28 11:15:45,960 WARNING SLOW CALL mempalace_diary_write write wait=0ms run=106753ms ok
2026-09-28 11:15:51,024 WARNING SLOW CALL mempalace_search read wait=104436ms run=5063ms ok
```

`wait=0ms` on the 36 s `status` is what told a cold page cache from lock contention; the last pair shows a 5 s search that spent 104 s queued behind a write. Neither distinction was visible before, and the timestamps are what let us match each line to a client "Request timed out" and prove the write had landed (the retry then filed a duplicate drawer).

### Environment

```
mempalace 3.9.0 (uv tool install), chromadb 1.5.9, Python 3.14.6, Windows 11 Pro.
Transport: mempalace serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765, two Claude Code HTTP clients.
Palace: 188,875 drawers, chroma.sqlite3 1.55 GB, embedding_metadata 2,845,774 rows.
```

problem_statement.title: Snowflake -> DuckDB: DATE_TRUNC on a DATE returns a TIMESTAMP
problem_statement.body:
**Fully reproducible code snippet**

`DATE_TRUNC` on a `DATE` returns a `DATE` in Snowflake but a `TIMESTAMP` in DuckDB, and the Snowflake to DuckDB transpilation passes the call through unchanged. Checked on `main` (feb0e08) with DuckDB 2.0.0:

```python
import duckdb, sqlglot

sql = sqlglot.transpile("SELECT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', CAST('2024-05-09' AS DATE))", read="snowflake", write="duckdb")[0]
print(sql)  # SELECT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', CAST('2024-05-09' AS DATE))

con = duckdb.connect()
print(con.execute(sql).fetchall(), con.description[0][1])
# [(datetime.datetime(2024, 5, 1, 0, 0),)] TIMESTAMP
```

On Snowflake the same query returns `datetime.date(2024, 5, 1)` as a `DATE` (checked on a live account, 10.38). The same applies to `TRUNC(<date>, 'MONTH')`, and to a time part on a date: `DATE_TRUNC('HOUR', <date>)` returns the date unchanged as a `DATE`.

Expected, when the argument is known to be a `DATE`: `SELECT CAST(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', CAST('2024-05-09' AS DATE)) AS DATE)` or equivalent.

**Official Documentation**

- Snowflake DATE_TRUNC: "The returned value is the same type as the input value." https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/date_trunc
- DuckDB `date_trunc(part, date)` returns `TIMESTAMP`: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/functions/date

problem_statement.title: `%pip` and `%uv` don't work in nushell if the path contains spaces
problem_statement.body:
Output of `python -c "import IPython; print(IPython.sys_info())"`:
```
{'commit_hash': '48ff029',
 'commit_source': 'installation',
 'default_encoding': 'utf-8',
 'ipython_path': '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with '
                 'spaces/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/IPython',
 'ipython_version': '9.17.1',
 'os_name': 'posix',
 'platform': 'macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O',
 'sys_executable': '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with '
                   'spaces/.venv/bin/python',
 'sys_platform': 'darwin',
 'sys_version': '3.14.8 (main, Oct  3 2026, 00:54:40) [Clang 22.1.3 ]'}
```

If the path of the notebook contains spaces, `%pip` and `%uv` magic commands don't work in [nushell](https://www.nushell.sh/). I guess this is due to differences in how escaping works since nushell is not a POSIX shell.

Here's a minimal reproducible example. When running `%pip install numpy`, I get
```
Error: nu::parser::parse_mismatch

  × Parse mismatch: expected operator.
   ╭─[source:1:69]
 1 │ '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with spaces/.venv/bin/python' -m pip install numpy
   ·                                                                     ─┬
   ·                                                                      ╰── expected operator
   ╰────
  help: Check the syntax around this position — a typo, missing delimiter, or
        wrong separator is common.

Note: you may need to restart the kernel to use updated packages.
```

To run an external command in nushell, a caret (^) in front of the string is needed, as per the [documentation](https://www.nushell.sh/book/working_with_strings.html#strings-as-external-commands). However, I saw that `IPython/core/magics/packaging.py` is using `shlex.quote(s)`, and [`shlex`'s documentation ](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html#shlex.quote) says it's only designed for Unix shells, so the same problem might occur in other shells. One possible fix could be using functions that pass command arguments with lists such as [subprocess.run()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) with `shell=False`.

problem_statement.title: Log a different error when Docker is unavailable on WSL2
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

Below what you currently see when Docker is unavailable on WSL2.
```
(venv) user@vm-win11:~/tmp/beeware/helloworld$ briefcase run --target ubuntu

*************************************************************************
** WARNING: Unable to determine if Docker is installed                 **
*************************************************************************

    Briefcase will proceed, assuming everything is OK. If you
    experience problems, this is almost certainly the cause of those
    problems.

    Please report this as a bug at:

      https://github.com/beeware/briefcase/issues/new

    In your report, please including the output from running:

      $ docker --version

    from the command prompt.

*************************************************************************

Briefcase was unable to use Docker commands. Check your Docker
installation, and try again.

Log saved to /home/user/tmp/beeware/helloworld/logs/briefcase.2024_02_04-17_57_53.run.log
```

Unfortunately, the current logic assumes that an unavailable Docker will raise an `OSError`.

But in WSL2, it returns a `CalledProcessError` with some useful text:
```
>>> exp = None
>>> try:
...     subprocess.check_output(["docker", "--version"])
... except Exception as e:
...     exp = e
...
>>> exp
CalledProcessError(1, ['docker', '--version'])
>>> exp.stdout
b"\nThe command 'docker' could not be found in this WSL 2 distro.\nWe recommend to activate the WSL integration in Docker Desktop settings.\n\nFor details about using Docker Desktop with WSL 2, visit:\n\nhttps://docs.docker.com/go/wsl2/\n\n"
```

Same thing happens at the bash prompt:
```
(venv) user@vm-win11:~/tmp/beeware/helloworld$ docker --version

The command 'docker' could not be found in this WSL 2 distro.
We recommend to activate the WSL integration in Docker Desktop settings.

For details about using Docker Desktop with WSL 2, visit:

https://docs.docker.com/go/wsl2/
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure Docker Desktop is not running
2. Run `briefcase build --target fedora`

### Expected behavior

Error handling provides a more useful message to the user.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Environment

- Operating System: Windows 11, WSL 2.0.14.0
- Python version: 3.8
- Software versions:
  - Briefcase: `0.3.17.dev283+g23daa64e`

### Logs

<details>

problem_statement.title: Optimizer removes CROSS JOIN inputs that are filtered empty or grouped into multiple rows
problem_statement.body:
**Before you file an issue**
- Read and write dialect: `duckdb`.
- Reproduced on current `main`, `b994fa759bb85182ae4a589c1d01973829236047`, with DuckDB 2.0.0. This uses the source checkout, not a released SQLGlot version.

An unused CROSS JOIN is removed even when its right side is empty or produces multiple groups. None of the failing examples below uses `LIMIT 1`, so these are separate cases from #8750.

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

```python
import duckdb
import sqlglot
from sqlglot.optimizer import optimize

con = duckdb.connect(':memory:')
con.execute('CREATE TABLE x(a INT); INSERT INTO x VALUES (1)')
con.execute('CREATE TABLE y(a INT); INSERT INTO y VALUES (1), (2)')
schema = {'x': {'a': 'INT'}, 'y': {'a': 'INT'}}

for rhs in [
    'SELECT 1 AS b WHERE FALSE',
    'SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y HAVING FALSE',
    'SELECT 1 AS b LIMIT 0',
    'SELECT 1 AS b OFFSET 1',
    'SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y GROUP BY y.a',
    'SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y WHERE FALSE',  # one-row control
    'SELECT 1 AS b',                          # one-row control
]:
    sql = 'SELECT x.a FROM x CROSS JOIN (' + rhs + ') AS z'
    optimized = optimize(
        sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read='duckdb'), schema=schema, dialect='duckdb'
    ).sql(dialect='duckdb')
    print(rhs)
    print('original:', con.execute(sql).fetchall())
    print('optimized:', con.execute(optimized).fetchall())
con.close()
```

Actual output:

```text
SELECT 1 AS b WHERE FALSE
original: []
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y HAVING FALSE
original: []
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT 1 AS b LIMIT 0
original: []
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT 1 AS b OFFSET 1
original: []
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y GROUP BY y.a
original: [(1,), (1,)]
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT COUNT(*) AS b FROM y WHERE FALSE
original: [(1,)]
optimized: [(1,)]
SELECT 1 AS b
original: [(1,)]
optimized: [(1,)]
```

Expected: the optimized and original rows should agree, including duplicates. The four empty right sides should keep the result empty. The grouped aggregate should retain both copies of `(1,)`. The last two examples are one-row controls and already agree.

The same five mismatches occur with `eliminate_joins` alone. `_has_single_output_row` accepts any FROM-less SELECT and any projection consisting entirely of aggregates, without accounting for filters, grouping, LIMIT 0, or OFFSET. A scalar aggregate without GROUP BY still produces one row on empty input, so a fix should preserve that control.

I checked this separately from the pending LIMIT-1 and DISTINCT-ON fixes. Reporting the reproducer first, as requested in CONTRIBUTING; I have not opened another PR for these cases.

**Official Documentation**
- [DuckDB GROUP BY](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/query_syntax/groupby)
- [DuckDB LIMIT and OFFSET](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/query_syntax/limit)

AI assistance: Codex and DeepSeek helped investigate this report. The code and output above were executed against the specified source revision and a real DuckDB connection.

problem_statement.title: `pdm show` leaves Homepage empty for packages that only set a Homepage Project-URL
problem_statement.body:
`ProjectInfo.from_distribution` takes the homepage only from the `Home-page` field. That field is deprecated, and a project that uses `[project.urls]` only gets `Project-URL` entries, so `pdm show rich` prints an empty Homepage right above its own Homepage URL:

```
Homepage:
Project URLs:          Documentation: https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
                       Homepage: https://github.com/Textualize/rich
```

The same code splits each `Project-URL` row on every comma. In core metadata the label ends at the first comma and the rest is the URL, which may contain commas itself. A row like `Docs, https://example.com/a,b` makes `pdm show` fail with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`.

problem_statement.title: Historical add_triple replay duplicates an identical closed validity interval
problem_statement.body:
**What happened?**
In an isolated MemPalace 3.10.0 pilot, retrying an identical closed historical relationship through `KnowledgeGraph.add_triple` produced two different IDs and two identical as-of results. Open-fact deduplication and supersession are separate cases.

This is a specific historical-interval continuation of the broader duplication concern in #655, not a claim that all graph inserts duplicate. Related #2268 / #2286 and #1139 concern open-fact provenance/reporting rather than replay of a closed interval.

**What did you expect?**
A supported way to replay the same historical source assertion after interruption without creating another logical assertion or losing its interval/provenance. Distinct recurring intervals and genuinely independent source assertions must remain distinguishable; unconditional subject/predicate/object deduplication would be incorrect.

Is `add_triple` intentionally append-only for closed intervals? If so, is there a supported historical import/replay API or stable assertion identity callers should use instead? Asking for the intended contract before proposing a patch.

**How to reproduce:**
The following reduces the executed synthetic pilot case (no private corpus):

```python
from mempalace.knowledge_graph import KnowledgeGraph

kg = KnowledgeGraph(":memory:")
kwargs = dict(
    valid_from="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    valid_to="2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
    source_closet="synthetic-replay-fixture",
)
first = kg.add_triple("Pilot History", "was", "Archived", **kwargs)
second = kg.add_triple("Pilot History", "was", "Archived", **kwargs)
rows = kg.query_entity("Pilot History", as_of="2025-01-15T00:00:00Z")
print(first == second, len(rows))
kg.close()
```

Executed file-backed pilot result: different IDs; two identical historical relationships persisted and returned by the as-of query. Database quick_check returned `ok`. The in-memory snippet is a reduction of that case, not a claim of a separately executed test.

**Source inspection:**
At develop commit `8c4865f70c49b6346c53474a9e5684c5f17d3fa9`, the duplicate lookup still selects only `valid_to IS NULL`; new IDs include filing time. That head was inspected, not installed/tested.

**Environment:**
- Linux
- Python 3.11 dedicated runtime
- MemPalace 3.10.0, stock SQLite knowledge graph

A useful acceptance case would preserve one logical assertion across an identical historical retry while retaining distinct validity intervals and source identities. No workaround or production data changes were made.

problem_statement.title: ui.sub_pages with root_path claims paths outside its root (e.g. /) because the prefix is stripped without checking
problem_statement.body:
### First Check

- [x] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [x] This is not a security issue (those should be reported via the [security advisory](https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/security/advisories/new) instead).
- [x] This is not a Q&A. I am sure something is wrong with NiceGUI or its documentation.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar [issue](https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/issues) and came up empty.

### Example Code

```python
from nicegui import APIRouter, app, ui


@ui.page('/')
def index():
    ui.label('Index page')


@ui.page('/other')
def other():
    ui.label('Other page')


router = APIRouter(prefix='/admin')


@router.page('/')
@router.page('/{path:path}')
def admin():
    ui.button('navigate.to("/")', on_click=lambda: ui.navigate.to('/'))
    ui.button('navigate.to("/other")', on_click=lambda: ui.navigate.to('/other'))
    ui.link('link to "/"', '/')
    ui.sub_pages({
        '/': lambda: ui.label('Admin overview'),
        '/users': lambda: ui.label('Admin users'),
    }, root_path='/admin')


app.include_router(router)

ui.run()
```

### Description

On a page with `ui.sub_pages(root_path='/admin')`, navigating to a path outside `/admin` does not leave the page if the rest of the path, after cutting off `len(root_path)` characters, matches one of the sub page routes. The URL changes, but the sub page content stays. This happens with `ui.navigate.to()` and with clicking a link.

Open `/admin/` and:

- click `navigate.to("/")`: the URL becomes `/`, the page still shows "Admin overview" (expected: "Index page")
- click `navigate.to("/other")`: the URL becomes `/other`, the page still shows "Admin overview" (expected: "Other page")
- click the link to `/`: same as the first case

Reloading the browser then shows the correct page.

The cause is in `SubPages._find_matching_path()` (`nicegui/elements/sub_pages.py`, line 147 in 3.18.0). It strips the root path by its length without checking that the current path starts with it:

```python
relative_path = self._router.current_path[len(self._root_path or ''):]
```

`'/'[6:]` and `'/other'[6:]` both give `''`. That is normalized to `'/'` and matches the sub page `'/'`. So `has_any_unresolved_path()` returns `False`, and `SubPagesRouter._handle_navigate()` (`sub_pages_router.py`, line 82) never calls `_other_page_builder_matches_path()`. It only pushes the new URL into the history.

Related but different: #5777 (fixed in #5886) and #6281 (fixed in #6374) both fixed the fallback in `_other_page_builder_matches_path()`, i.e. finding the other page once `ui.sub_pages` has given up on a path. Here `ui.sub_pages` never gives up, because the path outside its `root_path` is wrongly matched by its own routes.

This is independent of #6281 / #6374. The other page would be found by `_other_page_builder_matches_path()`, but that method is never reached. The behavior is the same with NiceGUI 3.17.0 and 3.18.0, and with FastAPI 0.140.6 and 0.142.4. For a target whose remainder does not match a sub page, for example `/other/page`, 3.18.0 correctly leaves the SPA.

A possible fix is to treat a path outside `root_path` as not matched:

```python
def _find_matching_path(self) -> RouteMatch | None:
    root_path = (self._root_path or '').rstrip('/')
    path = urlparse(self._router.current_path).path
    if root_path and path != root_path and not path.startswith(root_path + '/'):
        return None
    ...  # unchanged
```

Then `_handle_navigate()` falls through to `_other_page_builder_matches_path()` and opens the other page. With `show_404=True`, `_set_match(None)` would briefly render the 404 label before the browser leaves. It may be nicer not to re-render at all for a path outside the root.

As a workaround we call `context.client.open(path)` instead of `ui.navigate.to(path)`. That does not help for links, for example in Markdown content.

### NiceGUI Version

3.18.0 (also 3.17.0)

### Python Version

3.10.11

### Browser

Edge

### Operating System

Windows

### Additional Context

_No response_

problem_statement.title: [bug] BatchSpanProcessor missing validation for export_timeout_millis <= 0
problem_statement.body:
### Describe your environment

OS: macOS / Linux
Python version: 3.10+
SDK version: main

### What happened?

In `opentelemetry-sdk` (`opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.BatchSpanProcessor` and `BatchLogRecordProcessor`), parameters like `max_queue_size`, `schedule_delay_millis`, and `max_export_batch_size` validate that values must be positive integers and raise a `ValueError` if `<= 0`.

However, `export_timeout_millis` is missing validation for values `<= 0`. Initializing `BatchSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter(), export_timeout_millis=-500)` or `export_timeout_millis=0` is accepted without raising a `ValueError`.

### Steps to Reproduce

from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, ConsoleSpanExporter

# 1. schedule_delay_millis correctly validates <= 0:
try:
    BatchSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter(), schedule_delay_millis=0)
except ValueError as e:
    print("schedule_delay_millis validation working:", e)

# 2. export_timeout_millis is missing validation:
bsp = BatchSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter(), export_timeout_millis=-500)
print("Accepted without ValueError!")

### Expected Result

Initializing `BatchSpanProcessor` or `BatchLogRecordProcessor` with `export_timeout_millis <= 0` should raise a `ValueError("export_timeout_millis must be positive.")`.

### Actual Result

Accepted without raising a `ValueError`.

### Additional context

Location: opentelemetry-sdk/src/opentelemetry/sdk/trace/export/__init__.py in `BatchSpanProcessor._validate_arguments()`.

I am opening a PR for this fix now!

### Would you like to implement a fix?

Yes

### Tip

<sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

problem_statement.title: bug(sdk): dsl.If string literals are not escaped in the compiled CEL condition
problem_statement.body:
### Environment

* KFP version: not deployment-specific. The condition is produced by the compiler and evaluated by the v2 driver (`backend/src/v2/expression`).
* KFP SDK version: built from `master` at `1f93df83e3d52235f696ccfde8893facfc99911b` (`kfp.__version__` reports `2.17.0`)
* All dependencies version: Python 3.13.9, protobuf 6.x; Go 1.27.3 with `github.com/google/cel-go v0.30.0` (from `go.mod`)

### What happened

When a `dsl.If` / `dsl.Elif` / `dsl.Condition` compares a channel with a string literal, the compiler inserts the literal into the CEL `triggerPolicy.condition` between single quotes without escaping it.

* A literal containing a single quote (for example `"it's"`) produces a condition that the backend cannot parse. The pipeline compiles and uploads successfully, and the driver then fails at run time with a CEL syntax error.
* A literal containing a backslash (for example `'C:\\temp'`, a Windows-style path) produces a condition that parses, but CEL reads `\t` as a tab escape. The condition evaluates to `false` even when the output is exactly `C:\temp`, so the branch is **silently skipped** with no error.

The compiler does not validate the condition string, so neither problem is visible until the pipeline runs.

### Steps to reproduce

`repro.py`:

```python
from kfp import compiler, dsl
import yaml


@dsl.component(base_image='python:3.11')
def produce() -> str:
    return "it's"


@dsl.component(base_image='python:3.11')
def noop():
    pass


@dsl.pipeline
def my_pipeline():
    t = produce()
    with dsl.If(t.output == "it's"):
        noop()
    with dsl.If(t.output == 'C:\\temp'):
        noop()


compiler.Compiler().compile(my_pipeline, 'pipeline.yaml')
tasks = yaml.safe_load(open('pipeline.yaml'))['root']['dag']['tasks']
for name, task in tasks.items():
    if 'triggerPolicy' in task:
        print(f"{name}: {task['triggerPolicy']['condition']}")
```

#### 1. Compiler output

Command: `PYTHONPATH=sdk/python python repro.py`

```
condition-1: inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'
condition-2: inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\temp'
```

#### 2. Backend evaluation of the compiled conditions

The two condition strings were copied verbatim into a test that calls `expression.New()` and `(*Expr).Condition`. These are the calls the driver makes in `backend/src/v2/driver/dag.go` and `backend/src/v2/driver/container.go`. In each case the input parameter is set to the value that should match.

<details><summary>backend/src/v2/expression/condition_escaping_repro_test.go</summary>

```go
package expression

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/api/v2alpha1/go/pipelinespec"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"
)

// Conditions copied verbatim from the compiled pipeline.yaml.
func TestConditionEscapingRepro(t *testing.T) {
	expr, err := New()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct{ value, condition string }{
		{"it's", `inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'`},
		{`C:\temp`, `inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\temp'`},
	} {
		input := &pipelinespec.ExecutorInput{Inputs: &pipelinespec.ExecutorInput_Inputs{
			ParameterValues: map[string]*structpb.Value{
				"pipelinechannel--produce-Output": structpb.NewStringValue(tc.value),
			},
		}}
		got, err := expr.Condition(input, tc.condition)
		t.Logf("value=%q condition=%s\n  -> result=%v err=%v", tc.value, tc.condition, got, err)
		if err != nil || !got {
			t.Errorf("expected condition to evaluate to true for value %q", tc.value)
		}
	}
}
```

</details>

Command: `go test ./backend/src/v2/expression/ -run TestConditionEscapingRepro -v`

```
=== RUN   TestConditionEscapingRepro
    condition_escaping_repro_test.go:26: value="it's" condition=inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'
          -> result=false err=ERROR: <input>:1:67: Syntax error: extraneous input 's' expecting <EOF>
         | inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'
         | ..................................................................^
        ERROR: <input>:1:68: Syntax error: token recognition error at: '''
         | inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'
         | ...................................................................^
    condition_escaping_repro_test.go:28: expected condition to evaluate to true for value "it's"
    condition_escaping_repro_test.go:26: value="C:\\temp" condition=inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\temp'
          -> result=false err=<nil>
    condition_escaping_repro_test.go:28: expected condition to evaluate to true for value "C:\\temp"
--- FAIL: TestConditionEscapingRepro (0.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/v2/expression	1.153s
FAIL
```

When the same test uses escaped literals (`'it\'s'` and `'C:\\temp'`), both conditions evaluate to `true`:

```
=== RUN   TestConditionEscapedForms
    condition_escaped_forms_test.go:26: value="it's" condition=inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it\'s'
          -> result=true err=<nil>
    condition_escaped_forms_test.go:26: value="C:\\temp" condition=inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\temp'
          -> result=true err=<nil>
--- PASS: TestConditionEscapedForms (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/v2/expression	0.861s
```

### Expected result

A string literal in a condition should be emitted as a CEL string literal with the same value. For the example above:

```
inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it\'s'
inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\temp'
```

If a pipeline compiles, its conditions should parse and evaluate in the backend with the same meaning as the Python comparison.

### Root cause

`sdk/python/kfp/compiler/pipeline_spec_builder.py`, `_single_binary_operation_to_cel_condition`. The string-literal branch formats the operand as `f"'{value_or_reference}'"` without escaping, so `'` ends the CEL literal early and `\` begins a CEL escape sequence. `_update_task_spec_for_condition_group` writes the result directly into `trigger_policy.condition`.

The existing `TestConditionLogic` tests in `sdk/python/kfp/compiler/compiler_test.py` assert exact condition strings, but only use literals without special characters (for example `'heads'`), so this case is not covered.

### Proposed regression test

Add cases to `TestConditionLogic` that assert the exact compiled condition for literals containing `'` and `\`. The following test was run against current `master`. It fails because of the unescaped literals and should pass once the literals are escaped:

```python
class TestConditionStringLiteralEscaping(unittest.TestCase):

    def _condition(self, literal):

        @dsl.pipeline
        def my_pipeline():
            with dsl.If(produce().output == literal):
                noop()

        return my_pipeline.pipeline_spec.root.dag.tasks[
            'condition-1'].trigger_policy.condition

    def test_single_quote_is_escaped(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            self._condition("it's"),
            "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it\\'s'",
        )

    def test_backslash_is_escaped(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            self._condition('C:\\temp'),
            "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\\\temp'",
        )
```

Command: `cd sdk/python && python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -W ignore kfp/compiler/condition_escaping_repro_test.py` (relevant lines of the output):

```
E       AssertionError: "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\temp'" != "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\\\temp'"
E       - inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\temp'
E       + inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'C:\\temp'
E       ?                                                                  +
E       AssertionError: "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'" != "inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it\\'s'"
E       - inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it's'
E       + inputs.parameter_values['pipelinechannel--produce-Output'] == 'it\'s'
E       ?                                                                  +
FAILED kfp/compiler/condition_escaping_repro_test.py::TestConditionStringLiteralEscaping::test_backslash_is_escaped
FAILED kfp/compiler/condition_escaping_repro_test.py::TestConditionStringLiteralEscaping::test_single_quote_is_escaped
============================== 2 failed in 0.34s ===============================
```

### Potential fix

Add a small helper in `pipeline_spec_builder.py` that escapes a Python string for a CEL single-quoted literal: `\` → `\\` first, then `'` → `\'`, plus control characters such as `\n`, `\r` and `\t`. Use it in the string-literal branch of `_single_binary_operation_to_cel_condition`. Conditions whose literals contain no special characters compile exactly as they do today, so the existing expected strings are unchanged.

### Materials and Reference

* #14814 / #14872 change the numeric-vs-boolean coercion in the same function. They do not touch the string-literal branch.
* CEL string literal escapes: https://github.com/cel-expr/cel-spec/blob/master/doc/langdef.md

---

problem_statement.title: Declarative config: `container` resource detector cannot be loaded
problem_statement.body:
### Describe your environment

OS: Linux (Docker image python:3.14-slim-bookworm)
Python version: Python 3.14.10
SDK version: 1.45.1
API version: 1.45.1
opentelemetry-configuration: 0.66b1
opentelemetry-resource-detector-containerid: 0.66b1

### What happened?

`container` is a detector name defined by the configuration schema (`ExperimentalResourceDetector` in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-configuration `schema/resource.yaml`, also used in its `otel-getting-started.yaml` example). 

Since #5129 it is looked up as an entry point named `container`, but the contrib package registers it as `containerid` (open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib#3536). 

So it never resolves, even with the package installed, and the SDK fails to start.

### Steps to Reproduce

In an empty directory:

```sh
cat > config.yml <<'EOF'
file_format: "1.0"
resource:
  detection/development:
    detectors:
      - container:
EOF
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -q opentelemetry-configuration==0.66b1 opentelemetry-resource-detector-containerid==0.66b1
.venv/bin/python -c 'from opentelemetry.configuration import configure_sdk, load_config_file; configure_sdk(load_config_file("config.yml"))'
```

### Expected Result

- `container` loads the contrib `ContainerResourceDetector` (as it did with #5004).
- If a detector can't be loaded, the SDK still starts: the schema says "Unrecognized names are ignored with a warning rather than failing SDK construction."

### Actual Result

ConfigurationError: Plugin 'container' not found in group 'opentelemetry_resource_detector'. Make sure the package providing this plugin is installed.

### Additional context

Hit while reusing the OpenTelemetry Demo's shared `otel-config.yml` (works for the Go service) in a Python service.

### Would you like to implement a fix?

Yes, I am open to it.

### Tip

<sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

problem_statement.title: refactor(csr): use pandas/xarray-style verbs for CSRLinearExpression and Grid methods
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

## Describe the feature you'd like to see

`linopy/csr.py` names the methods of `CSRLinearExpression` and `Grid` as past participles (`summed`, `renamed`, `reindexed`, ...). They return a new frozen object, never mutate. pandas and xarray use plain verbs for the same copy-returning operations (`df.rename`, `da.reindex`, `fillna`, ...), so the CSR layer diverges from the convention of the ecosystem linopy builds on.

Proposal: rename them to pandas/xarray-style verbs. Pure refactor, no behavior change.

| current | proposed |
|---|---|
| `CSRLinearExpression.summed(dims)` | `sum(dims)` |
| `aggregated(grid, rows)` | `aggregate(grid, rows)` |
| `renamed(names)` | `rename(names)` |
| `reindexed(grid, fill)` | `reindex(grid, fill)` |
| `filled(value)` | `fillna(value)` |
| `taken(rows, grid)` | `take(rows, grid)` |
| `added(other)` | `add(other)` |
| `scaled(factor)` | `mul(factor)` |
| `contracted(...)` | `dot(...)` |
| `pruned()` | `prune()` |
| `with_const(const)` | `assign_const(const)` (or keep) |
| `Grid.renamed` / `reordered` / `conformed` / `combined` | `rename` / `transpose` / `conform` / `combine` |

```python
# today
expr._csr.aggregated(grid, rows).filled(0.0)
expr._csr.scaled(-1.0)
# proposed
expr._csr.aggregate(grid, rows).fillna(0.0)
expr._csr.mul(-1.0)
```

**Trade-off to decide:** `LinearExpression` already exposes the xarray verbs publicly. After the rename, `expr.sum()` and `expr._csr.sum()` share a name but differ in signature and semantics (e.g. the CSR `sum` takes a grid-level dim list and keeps explicit zero coefficients). The current participles keep the internal sparse layer visibly separate from the public dense API. The `_csr` attribute and the `CSRLinearExpression` type arguably mark that boundary well enough on their own.

--- a/docs/flow/README.md
+++ b/docs/flow/README.md
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 # Materialization Flow Docs
 
-_Last updated: 2026-09-30_
+_Last updated: 2026-10-22_
 
 These docs map how each dbt-databricks materialization executes — the decision branches, the
 order of operations, and where shared logic (like relation replacement) is reused. They are
@@ -33,6 +33,28 @@ Materializations that honor the flag show both diagrams in their doc:
 | Materialized view | [materialized_view_flow.md](materialized_view_flow.md) | No — single path |
 | _(shared)_ Relation replacement | [replace_flow.md](replace_flow.md) | Used by view, materialized-view, streaming-table, and metric-view replacement helpers |
 
+## Hook transaction categories
+
+dbt splits hooks into an inside-transaction category (unset or `transaction: true`) and an
+outside-transaction category (`transaction: false`, including `before_begin` / `after_commit`).
+Pre-hooks run outside then inside; post-hooks run inside then outside. dbt-databricks overrides
+`run_hooks` (`materializations/hooks.sql`) because the adapter never opens a transaction, and the
+global macro's literal `commit;` before the outside category fails on Databricks.
+
+The `use_non_transactional_hooks` behavior flag (defined as
+[`USE_NON_TRANSACTIONAL_HOOKS`](../../dbt/adapters/databricks/impl.py)) controls the outside
+category. It **defaults to `False`**: those hooks are skipped without rendering their SQL, and dbt
+emits its behavior-change warning once per invocation, only if a skipped hook was encountered.
+When enabled, they run at their outside-transaction position with no `COMMIT`.
+
+The inherited function (UDF) materialization is an exception: it invokes only the
+inside-transaction hook category, so its `transaction: false` hooks remain skipped without a
+warning even when this flag is enabled.
+
+Inside-transaction hooks are unaffected. Each diagram's hook steps keep their existing positions, so
+materialized views and streaming tables still run the outside category on no-op branches that skip
+the inside category.
+
 ## Not yet documented
 
 These have macros but no dedicated flow doc yet: **metric view**, **clone**, and **Python models**

+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+import pytest
+from dbt_common.behavior_flags import Behavior
+from dbt_common.events.types import BehaviorChangeEvent
+from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader
+
+from dbt.adapters.databricks.impl import USE_NON_TRANSACTIONAL_HOOKS
+
+ORDINARY = {"sql": "ordinary hook", "transaction": True}
+OUTSIDE = {"sql": "outside hook", "transaction": False}
+ORDINARY_EVENTS = [("render", "ordinary hook"), ("statement", "ordinary hook", True)]
+OUTSIDE_EVENTS = [("render", "outside hook"), ("statement", "outside hook", False)]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fired_events():
+    with patch("dbt_common.behavior_flags.fire_event") as fire_event:
+        yield fire_event
+
+
+def make_hooks_module(behavior, pre_hooks=(), post_hooks=()):
+    events = []
+
+    def statement(auto_begin, caller):
+        events.append(("statement", caller().strip(), auto_begin))
+        return ""
+
+    def render(sql):
+        events.append(("render", sql))
+        return sql
+
+    context = {
+        "statement": statement,
+        "render": render,
+        "adapter": Mock(behavior=behavior),
+        "pre_hooks": list(pre_hooks),
+        "post_hooks": list(post_hooks),
+    }
+    env = Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader("dbt/include/databricks/macros/materializations"))
+    return env.get_template("hooks.sql").make_module(context), events
+
+
+def behavior(flag_enabled=None):
+    overrides = {} if flag_enabled is None else {"use_non_transactional_hooks": flag_enabled}
+    return Behavior([USE_NON_TRANSACTIONAL_HOOKS], overrides)
+
+
+def behavior_change_events(fired_events):
+    events = [c.args[0] for c in fired_events.call_args_list]
+    return [event for event in events if isinstance(event, BehaviorChangeEvent)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("flag_enabled", [None, False], ids=["default", "explicit-false"])
+def test_outside_hooks_skipped_with_one_warning_per_invocation(fired_events, flag_enabled):
+    hooks, events = make_hooks_module(
+        behavior(flag_enabled), pre_hooks=[OUTSIDE, ORDINARY], post_hooks=[ORDINARY, OUTSIDE]
+    )
+    for _ in range(2):
+        hooks.run_pre_hooks()
+        hooks.run_post_hooks()
+
+    assert events == ORDINARY_EVENTS * 4
+    warnings = behavior_change_events(fired_events)
+    assert len(warnings) == 1
+    assert warnings[0].flag_name == "use_non_transactional_hooks"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("phase", ["pre", "post"])
+def test_outside_hooks_run_without_commit_when_flag_enabled(fired_events, phase):
+    hooks, events = make_hooks_module(behavior(True), **{f"{phase}_hooks": [ORDINARY, OUTSIDE]})
+    getattr(hooks, f"run_{phase}_hooks")()
+
+    expected = (
+        OUTSIDE_EVENTS + ORDINARY_EVENTS if phase == "pre" else ORDINARY_EVENTS + OUTSIDE_EVENTS
+    )
+    assert events == expected
+    assert behavior_change_events(fired_events) == []
+
+
+def test_ordinary_hooks_only_do_not_warn(fired_events):
+    hooks, events = make_hooks_module(behavior(), pre_hooks=[ORDINARY], post_hooks=[ORDINARY])
+    hooks.run_pre_hooks()
+    hooks.run_post_hooks()
+
+    assert events == ORDINARY_EVENTS * 2
+    assert behavior_change_events(fired_events) == []
+
+

+    hooks, events = make_hooks_module(behavior(), pre_hooks=[{"sql": "  ", "transaction": True}])
+    hooks.run_pre_hooks()

+    assert events == [("render", "  ")]

problem_statement.title: transaction: false model/seed hooks are not honored (silently skipped on default path, error on v2/seed/metric_view)
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

A model or seed hook configured with `transaction: false` (e.g. `pre_hook={'sql': '...', 'transaction': false}`) is not run the way the user intends on dbt-databricks. The failure mode depends on the materialization path:

- **Default path** (`use_materialization_v2 = false`, the default — `table` / `view` / `incremental`): the `transaction: false` hook is **silently skipped**. No error, no log line — it simply never executes.
- **`use_materialization_v2 = true`, and seeds, and metric views**: the run **fails** with:
  ```
  [NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION] There is no active transaction to commit.
  ```

Default-transaction hooks (`transaction: true` or unset) work correctly in both cases. The model/seed config itself is parsed correctly — the issue is in how the materializations execute hooks.

### Steps To Reproduce

A model with a `transaction: false` hook is enough. Minimal repro:

```sql
-- models/hook_demo.sql
{{ config(
    materialized='table',
    pre_hook=[
        "create table if not exists {{ this.schema }}.hook_audit (marker string)",
        {"sql": "insert into {{ this.schema }}.hook_audit values ('txn_true')",  "transaction": true},
        {"sql": "insert into {{ this.schema }}.hook_audit values ('txn_false')", "transaction": false}
    ]
) }}
select 1 as id
```

```bash
dbt run -s hook_demo
# then inspect:
#   select * from <schema>.hook_audit;
```

- **Default config:** `dbt run` succeeds, but `hook_audit` contains only `txn_true` — the `txn_false` row is missing. The `transaction: false` hook never ran.
- **With `flags: {use_materialization_v2: true}` in `dbt_project.yml`** (or for a seed / metric view): `dbt run` **fails** with `[NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION] There is no active transaction to commit.`

### Expected behavior

Because Databricks has no transactions, a model's pre/post hooks should run **regardless** of their `transaction` setting — a `transaction: false` hook should execute exactly once, like a default hook. (This is the stated intent of dbt-databricks's `run_pre_hooks` / `run_post_hooks` override, which calls `run_hooks` for both `inside_transaction` passes.)

### Screenshots and log output

`use_materialization_v2 = true` (or seed / metric view) path — the run errors on the `commit;` that dbt-core's `run_hooks` emits for the outside-transaction pass:

```
Databricks adapter: Exception while trying to execute query
        commit;
: [NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION] There is no active transaction to commit.
  ... com.databricks.sql.transaction.tahoe.DeltaUnsupportedOperationException:
      [NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION] There is no active transaction to commit.
  ... com.databricks.sql.transaction.tahoe.commands.CommitTransactionCommand.run(CommitTransactionCommand.scala:76)

Database Error in model hook_demo (models/hook_demo.sql)
  [NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION] There is no active transaction to commit.
```

Default path: no error; the `transaction: false` insert is simply absent from the generated SQL.

### System information

**The output of `dbt --version`:**
```
Core:
  - installed: 1.11.11
Plugins:
  - databricks: 1.12.1
  - spark: 1.10.1
```

**The operating system you're using:** macOS (reproduced on a serverless SQL warehouse; the cause is SQL/macro-level, so any Databricks compute is affected)

**The output of `python --version`:** Python 3.10.20

### Additional context

Root cause (with file references in this repo):

dbt-core's `run_hooks(hooks, inside_transaction)` splits hooks by their `transaction` flag (`selectattr('transaction', 'equalto', inside_transaction)`; default `True`) and, for the `inside_transaction=False` pass, emits a literal `commit;` before the first hook. Databricks/Delta has no transactions and rejects a bare `commit;` (`[NO_ACTIVE_TRANSACTION]`).

dbt-databricks calls hooks two inconsistent ways:

| Materialization | Path | Hook call | `transaction: false` result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table.sql` | v2 (`run_pre_hooks`/`run_post_hooks`, lines 17/43) | calls `inside_transaction=False` pass | **error** (`commit;`) |
| `table.sql` | **v1 (default)** `run_hooks(pre_hooks)` (45/77) | default `inside_transaction=True` | **silently skipped** |
| `view.sql` | v2 (10/42) / **v1 (45/69)** | same | error / **silent skip** |
| `incremental.sql` | v2 (30/92) / **v1 (102/219)** | same | error / **silent skip** |
| `seeds.sql` | v1 (71/74,104/109) & v2 (29/51) | both reach `inside_transaction=False` | **error** |
| `metric_view.sql` | always `run_pre_hooks`/`run_post_hooks` (8/38) | calls `inside_transaction=False` pass | **error** |

`use_materialization_v2` defaults to `False` (`dbt/adapters/databricks/impl.py`), so the silent-skip path is the default user experience. The `commit;` reaches the server as raw SQL via `statement` → `add_query` → `handle.execute("commit;")`, bypassing the adapter's already-no-op `commit()`.

**Suggested fix:** override the global `run_hooks` macro in dbt-databricks to run all hooks in a single pass with no `transaction` split and no `commit;` preamble (Databricks has no transaction to commit). This is the only single change that covers both failure modes everywhere, since the v1 `else` branches call `run_hooks` directly (not the `run_pre_hooks`/`run_post_hooks` wrappers). Overriding only the wrappers fixes the error paths but not the v1 silent-skip; a connection-layer `commit;` no-op fixes the error paths but not the silent-skip. The v1/v2 hook paths should also be unified for consistency.

problem_statement.body:
### First Check

- [x] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [x] This is not a security issue.
- [x] This is not a Q&A. I am sure something is wrong with NiceGUI or its documentation.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar issue and came up empty.

### Example Code

```python
import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from nicegui import app, background_tasks, ui

OUT = Path('shutdown_probe.txt')
OUT.unlink(missing_ok=True)


@background_tasks.await_on_shutdown
async def save(tag: str) -> None:
    await asyncio.sleep(3)  # still in flight when the shutdown below fires
    with OUT.open('a') as f:
        f.write(tag + '\n')


async def stop_soon() -> None:
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    app.shutdown()


app.on_startup(lambda: save('on_startup'))  # works
app.on_connect(lambda: save('on_connect'))  # broken
app.on_startup(stop_soon)

ui.label('open this page once, then wait a few seconds')
ui.run(reload=False)
```

### Description

`@background_tasks.await_on_shutdown` is documented as *"Tag an async function so tasks created from it won't be cancelled during shutdown."* That holds for `app.on_startup`, but **not** for handlers invoked in a client context — they are cancelled at shutdown anyway, silently.

Run the snippet above, let the page load once, and wait for the automatic shutdown. `shutdown_probe.txt` should contain both lines. Actual output:

```
on_startup
```

`on_connect` is missing. Both went through the same decorator; only the one that did not pass through a client context survived. `on_startup` here is the control — it proves shutdown really does await protected work, so the difference is not the grace period.

I measured three affected entry points, all still cancelled:

| entry point | dispatch path |
|---|---|
| `app.on_connect(handler)` / `client.on_connect(...)` | `Client.safe_invoke` |
| `ui.button(on_click=handler)` | `handle_event` |
| `ui.timer(0.01, handler, once=True)` | `Timer` |

### Mechanism

`background_tasks.create()` recognises protected work by identity:

https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/blob/main/nicegui/background_tasks.py#L47

Every context-preserving dispatch path wraps the awaitable in a **fresh coroutine** before calling `create()`, so that `isinstance` check no longer matches:

- `nicegui/client.py:455` and `:482` — `helpers.await_with_context(result, ...)`
- `nicegui/events.py:486` — `_await_and_handle_in_context(result, parent_slot)`
- `nicegui/timer.py:45` — `coroutine()`

`App.safe_invoke` (`nicegui/app/app.py:110`) passes `result` straight through, which is why `on_startup` is the one that works.

This is **not a regression** — I checked, expecting one. `#5879` replaced a hand-rolled `async def result_with_client()` wrapper in `safe_invoke` with the shared `await_with_context` helper, but the old code wrapped the awaitable too, so the marker was already being hidden. The behaviour dates back to `@await_on_shutdown` and `safe_invoke` first coexisting, and reproduces on `v3.16.0`.

Worth noting the documented example works, which is probably why this has gone unnoticed — [`section_configuration_deployment.py:186`](https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/blob/main/website/documentation/content/section_configuration_deployment.py#L186) uses `on_click=lambda: background_tasks.create(backup())`, and that extra `lambda` hands `create()` the marker directly. Only the shorthand `on_click=backup` fails.

I have not proposed a fix — whether the marker should be propagated through the wrappers, detected differently, or the docstring narrowed to match feels like your call.

### NiceGUI Version

3.16.0 (also reproduced on `main`)

### Python Version

3.14.0

### Browser

Chrome

### Operating System

macOS

### Additional Context

Found while reviewing #6329, which fixes the same *class* of marker loss one layer down (a requeued lazy task losing its protection). That PR's fix does not cover these paths — I re-measured all three against its branch and they are still cancelled.
