problem_statement.title: [Bug]: 邮箱 name 字段含完整地址时，mail monitor 拼成 name@domain@domain 导致 AUTHENTICATIONFAILED（升级后老配置失效）
problem_statement.body:
**TL;DR (EN)**
The mail monitor builds the IMAP login name as `f"{credential.name}@{credential.domain}"`, but an existing mailbox configured with the **full address in `name`** (e.g. `name="3855686217@qq.com"`, `domain="qq.com"`) produces `3855686217@qq.com@qq.com` → `[AUTHENTICATIONFAILED]` from the provider. The credential itself is valid.

---

### 环境

- QwenPaw `2.2.2.post1`（Docker）
- 邮箱：QQ 邮箱 `3855686217@qq.com`，IMAP/SMTP 已开启，授权码有效
- 该邮箱账号是 **2026-10-21 配置**的（`mail_state/3855686217_at_qq.com/` 建于 10-21 21:14）

### 现象

`qwenpaw.log` 自 **2026-10-22 18:09** 起持续报错，每 120 秒重试一次：

```
WARNING | qwenpaw/app/mail/monitor.py:1528 | mail monitor poll error for agent kTpb23;
retrying in 120s: b'[AUTHENTICATIONFAILED] Login fail. Account is abnormal, service is
not open, password is incorrect, login frequency limited, or system is busy.
More information at https://help.mail.qq.com/detail/108/1023'
```

### 排查结论（问题不在授权码，也不在邮箱服务商）

同一台机器、同一份凭据，直接用 Python 登录是**成功**的：

```
IMAP4_SSL("imap.qq.com", 993).login("3855686217@qq.com", <auth_code>)
→ ('OK', [b'Success login ok'])
→ INBOX: OK [b'529']
SMTP smtp.qq.com:465 → 认证通过
```

而用 monitor 自己拼出来的账号名登录，报的错误**与日志一字不差**：

```
login("3855686217@qq.com@qq.com", <auth_code>)
→ error b'[AUTHENTICATIONFAILED] Login fail. Account is abnormal, ...'
```

### 根因

`qwenpaw/app/mail/monitor.py:1096`：

```python
self.email_address = f"{credential.name}@{credential.domain}"
```

而 `agent.json` 里存的是：

```json
"mail": { "credential": { "name": "3855686217@qq.com", "domain": "qq.com", "provider": "" } }
```

`name` 里已经带了完整地址，于是拼成 `name@domain@domain`。
`pydantic` 的 `AgentMailCredential.name` 没有校验"不得包含 `@`"，`_validate_mail_config()` 也没拦，所以这种配置能一直存在并在启动时被原样使用。

时间点也对得上：10-21 配置时是旧语义（`name` 直接当账号），10-22 升级到 2.2.x 后 start building `name@domain`，老配置就全挂了。

### 另外一个连带坑（同一个字段）

`credentials.yaml` 的 `public.name` 参与身份比对：

```python
if record.public and record.public != _agent_mail_public_identity(mail):
    return mail      # 身份不一致就不注入 auth_code
```

把 `name` 从 `3855686217@qq.com` 改成 `3855686217` 时，如果 YAML 里没加引号写成 `name: 3855686217`，会被解析成 **int**，而 `agent.json` 里是 **str** → 比对失败 → `auth_code` 不注入 → MCP 报 `Missing required environment variables QWENPAWMAIL_EMAIL and/or QWENPAWMAIL_AUTH_CODE`，看起来像"凭据丢了"，其实还在。建议 `_agent_mail_public_identity()` 对 `name` 做 str 归一化，或不把纯数字字符串写进 YAML 时省略引号。

### 建议

1. `_validate_mail_config()` 增加校验：`name` 含 `@` 时要么报错、要么自动拆成 `name/domain`（对老配置做一次迁移最友好）；
2. 或者在 `monitor.py` 里防御：`if "@" in credential.name: email_address = credential.name`；
3. `_agent_mail_public_identity()` 里对 `name`/`domain` 做 `str()` 归一化，避免 int/str 比对失败；
4. 顺便：`public.name` 与 `agent.json` 不一致时目前是**静默跳过**（日志里没有任何提示），这类"凭据静默失效"很难排查，建议至少打一条 WARNING。

### 临时处理（我这边已生效）

`agent.json` → `mail.credential.name = "3855686217"`；`credentials.yaml` → `name: '3855686217'`（带引号）。之后：

```
INFO | mail/monitor.py:1207 | mail monitor started for agent kTpb23 (3855686217@qq.com, mode=agent_all)
```

报错归零，MCP `qwenpawmail` 也恢复正常。

title: fix(jinja): support dbt materialization blocks in the Jinja templater
issue_title: Dbt custom materialization macro raise error with jinja templater and is skipped with dbt templater

install_config.install: pip install -e . -q && pip install -r requirements_dev.txt -q && pip install -e plugins/sqlfluff-plugin-example -q

gold_patch:
diff --git a/docsv/configuration/templating/jinja.md b/docsv/configuration/templating/jinja.md
index 7c5cf66ef6..bb815d8c55 100644
--- a/docsv/configuration/templating/jinja.md
+++ b/docsv/configuration/templating/jinja.md
@@ -225,6 +225,10 @@ projects. In particular it provides mock objects for:
   linting purposes, this makes no difference and so the provided macro simply
   returns nothing.
 
+It also understands the dbt `{% test %}` and `{% materialization %}` blocks,
+so files which define generic tests or custom materializations can be linted
+like other macro files.
+
 ::: tip NOTE
 If there are other builtin macros which would make your life easier,
 consider submitting the idea (or even better a pull request) on [github](https://www.github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff).

--- a/src/sqlfluff/core/templaters/jinja.py
+++ b/src/sqlfluff/core/templaters/jinja.py

-        and all(t in (ExprStmtExtension, DBTTestExtension) for t in extension_types)
+        and all(
+            t in (ExprStmtExtension, DBTTestExtension, DBTMaterializationExtension)
+            for t in extension_types

         and _holds_same_objects(env.tests, _JINJA_TESTS)
         and env.policies == _JINJA_POLICIES
@@ -526,9 +529,9 @@ def _get_jinja_env(self, config: Optional[FluffConfig] = None) -> Environment:
         get_source method to handle missing templates when templating is ignored.
         If 'ignore' is not present or does not contain 'templating', it uses the
         regular FileSystemLoader. It then sets the extensions to ['jinja2.ext.do']
-        and adds the DBTTestExtension if the _apply_dbt_builtins method returns
-        True. Finally, it returns a SandboxedEnvironment object with the
-        specified settings.
+        and adds the DBTTestExtension and DBTMaterializationExtension if the
+        _apply_dbt_builtins method returns True. Finally, it returns a
+        SandboxedEnvironment object with the specified settings.
 
         Args:
             config (dict, optional): A dictionary containing configuration settings.
@@ -569,6 +572,7 @@ def get_source(
         environment_class = SandboxedEnvironment
         if self._apply_dbt_builtins(config):
             extensions.append(DBTTestExtension)
+            extensions.append(DBTMaterializationExtension)
             environment_class = DbtSandboxedEnvironment
 
         return environment_class(
@@ -1439,3 +1443,60 @@ def parse(self, parser: jinja2.parser.Parser) -> jinja2.nodes.Macro:
         node.name = f"test_{test_name}"
         node.body = parser.parse_statements(("name:endtest",), drop_needle=True)
         return node
+
+
+class DBTMaterializationExtension(Extension):
+    """Jinja extension to handle the dbt materialization tag.
+
+    dbt defines custom materializations with a block of the form
+    ``{% materialization <name>, adapter='<adapter>' %}`` (or ``default``
+    instead of ``adapter=...``), which it compiles into a macro called
+    ``materialization_<name>_<adapter>``.
+    """
+
+    tags = {"materialization"}
+
+    def parse(self, parser: jinja2.parser.Parser) -> jinja2.nodes.Macro:
+        """Parses out the contents of the materialization tag."""
+        node = jinja2.nodes.Macro(lineno=next(parser.stream).lineno)
+        materialization_name = parser.parse_assign_target(name_only=True).name
+        adapter_name = "default"
+        node.args = []
+        node.defaults = []
+
+        while parser.stream.skip_if("comma"):
+            target = parser.parse_assign_target(name_only=True)
+            if target.name == "default":
+                continue
+            elif target.name == "adapter":
+                parser.stream.expect("assign")
+                adapter = parser.parse_expression()
+                if not isinstance(adapter, jinja2.nodes.Const):
+                    parser.fail(
+                        "The adapter of a materialization must be a literal.",
+                        adapter.lineno,
+                    )
+                adapter_name = str(adapter.value)
+            elif target.name == "supported_languages":
+                # dbt passes this to the materialization macro as a parameter.
+                target.set_ctx("param")
+                node.args.append(target)
+                parser.stream.expect("assign")
+                node.defaults.append(parser.parse_expression())
+            else:
+                parser.fail(
+                    f"Unexpected argument {target.name!r} for materialization "
+                    f"{materialization_name!r}.",
+                    target.lineno,
+                )
+
+        if not any(arg.name == "supported_languages" for arg in node.args):
+            # Like dbt, default to a materialization which only supports SQL.
+            node.args.append(jinja2.nodes.Name("supported_languages", "param"))
+            node.defaults.append(jinja2.nodes.List([jinja2.nodes.Const("sql")]))
+
+        node.name = f"materialization_{materialization_name}_{adapter_name}"
+        node.body = parser.parse_statements(
+            ("name:endmaterialization",), drop_needle=True
+        )
+        return node

problem_statement.title: nanoseconds_to_str() drops a microsecond through float rounding (2.3 s prints as 0:00:02.299999)
problem_statement.body:
### pipecat version

`main` (1.14.1.dev)

### Description

`pipecat.utils.time.nanoseconds_to_str()` converts the nanosecond count to float seconds and then pulls the microseconds back out with `(total_seconds - int(total_seconds)) * 1_000_000`. Floating-point error makes that truncate down by one microsecond for many ordinary values, so the formatted string is wrong. This is what `Frame.__str__` uses to print a frame's `pts`, so logs and observers show slightly wrong timestamps.

### Reproduction

```python
from pipecat.utils.time import nanoseconds_to_str

print(nanoseconds_to_str(2_300_000_000))      # 0:00:02.299999  (expected 0:00:02.300000)
print(nanoseconds_to_str(1_000_001_000))      # 0:00:01.000000  (expected 0:00:01.000001)
print(nanoseconds_to_str(3_600_000_001_000))  # 1:00:00.000000  (expected 1:00:00.000001)
```

### Expected

The hours/minutes/seconds/microseconds split should be done with integer arithmetic on the nanosecond value, so exact values print exactly (sub-microsecond digits still truncated, as today).

I have a fix with tests ready and will open a PR.

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: SBOM upstream entry uses the `purl.version` value when `purl.upstream` is not set
problem_statement.body:
**Related:** #1370, #1371

## Why this is a bug

The `purl.version` setting changes the version of the wheel entry (`SPDXRef-wheel`) in the SBOM.
If `purl.upstream` is not set, `purl.version` also changes the version of the upstream entry (`SPDXRef-upstream`).
PR #1371 did not change the upstream entry. The problem continues after PR #1371.

- The upstream entry identifies the source that fromager used. The upstream project released `0.5.5`.
  The upstream project did not release `0.5.5+local.1`.
- The `GENERATED_FROM` relationship points from the wheel to the upstream entry.
  As a result, the relationship points to a version that does not exist upstream.
- Tools that use this relationship cannot find the upstream release.
- If `sbom.repository_url` is not set, the two entries have the same purl.
  Then the SBOM does not show a difference between the wheel and its source.
- The `purl.upstream` setting prevents this problem. But fromager does not tell users that this setting is necessary.
- The tests that PR #1371 added set `purl.upstream`. Because of this, the tests do not find this problem.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install fromager from the `main` branch, at commit `45241aad` or a later commit.
   Fromager 0.101.0 also shows the problem.
2. Make the file `overrides/settings.yaml` with this content:

   ```yaml
   sbom:
     supplier: "Organization: ExampleCo"
     namespace: "https://sbom.example"
   ```

3. Make the file `overrides/settings/sqlparse.yaml` with this content:

   ```yaml
   purl:
     version: "0.5.5+local.1"
   ```

4. Do not set `purl.upstream`.
5. Build the wheel:

   ```bash
   fromager bootstrap sqlparse==0.5.5
   ```

6. Show the SBOM values of the upstream entry:

   ```bash
   WHL=$(ls wheels-repo/downloads/sqlparse-*.whl)
   unzip -p "$WHL" '*.dist-info/sboms/fromager.spdx.json' \
     | jq '.packages[1] | .versionInfo, .externalRefs[0].referenceLocator'
   ```

7. Compare the values with the correct values.

   Actual values:

   ```text
   "0.5.5+local.1"
   "pkg:pypi/sqlparse@0.5.5%2Blocal.1"
   ```

   Correct values:

   ```text
   "0.5.5"
   "pkg:pypi/sqlparse@0.5.5"
   ```

problem_statement.title: [BUG] add_mjcf drops spatial-tendon sites whose names contain "-"
problem_statement.body:
**Version:** newton 1.6.1 (warp-lang 1.18.0, mujoco 3.12.0), CPU. The same code is on `main`: site labels keep the raw name (`site_label = f"{label_prefix}/{site_name}"`).

**What happens:** a spatial tendon loses every site whose name contains `-`. `add_mjcf` warns `Spatial tendon 'flexor' references unknown site 'm_origin', skipping element.` and then drops the tendon (`has no valid wrap elements`). The same model with `_` instead of `-` imports without warnings.

**Reproduction:**

```python
import warnings
import newton

XML = """<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="upper">
      <geom type="capsule" fromto="0 0 0 0 0 -0.3" size="0.03"/>
      <site name="m-origin" pos="0.02 0 -0.05"/>
      <body name="lower" pos="0 0 -0.3">
        <joint name="elbow" axis="0 1 0"/>
        <geom type="capsule" fromto="0 0 0 0 0 -0.25" size="0.025"/>
        <site name="m-insertion" pos="0.02 0 -0.05"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
  <tendon>
    <spatial name="flexor">
      <site site="m-origin"/>
      <site site="m-insertion"/>
    </spatial>
  </tendon>
</mujoco>"""

builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    builder.add_mjcf(XML)
print([str(w.message) for w in caught])  # unknown site 'm_origin', 'm_insertion'
```

**Likely cause** (from `newton/_src/utils/import_mjcf.py` in 1.6.1): the spatial-tendon parser sanitizes the referenced name (`site_name = sanitize_name(site_name)`, which turns `-` into `_`), then looks it up with `find_shape_by_name`, which compares against `builder.shape_label`. The labels keep the original name (`m-origin`), so the sanitized name never matches. The site-equality path uses `site_name_to_idx`, which is keyed by the sanitized name and would find the site.

**Impact:** MyoSuite's musculoskeletal models (elbow, hand, arm, leg, and the MuscleMimic full body and bimanual) name their muscle path sites with hyphens, so their muscle-tendon paths lose sites on import. Context: #238.

problem_statement.body:
### What happened? (You can include a screenshot if it helps explain)

In gui, design matrix is merged both on panel start, and also when an experiment is ran.
This has the consequence of silently overwriting any potential edits of parameters and update strategies done in GUI.
Merging parameters IS NOT idempotent.

### What did you expect to happen?

Parameters from design matrix should only be merged once.

_No response_

problem_statement.title: Constant LinearExpression * multi-term LinearExpression raises TypeError (mirrored product works)
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

### Version Checks

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the current `master` branch of Linopy (95f6bfa4).

### Issue Description

Multiplying a constant `LinearExpression` (no terms) by a multi-term `LinearExpression` raises `TypeError` on both the dense and sparse backends. The mirrored product (multi-term × constant) and constant × one-term expression both work and return the scaled linear expression.

Cause: `LinearExpression._multiply_by_linear_expression` checks `other.nterm > 1` and raises *before* checking `self.is_constant`. `__mul__` then turns that `TypeError` into `NotImplemented`, so the user only sees the generic `unsupported operand type(s)` message.

Found while building the dense/sparse conformance suite for #1019.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import warnings
from linopy import LinearExpression, Model

warnings.simplefilter("ignore")  # PerformanceWarning on sparse
for sparse in (False, True):
    m = Model(sparse=sparse)
    x = m.add_variables(name="x")
    y = m.add_variables(name="y")
    c = LinearExpression(3, m)
    print(f"sparse={sparse}")
    for lab, f in {
        "c * (2*x + 3*y)": lambda: c * (2 * x + 3 * y),
        "(2*x + 3*y) * c": lambda: (2 * x + 3 * y) * c,
        "c * (2*x)": lambda: c * (2 * x),
        "3 * (2*x + 3*y)": lambda: 3 * (2 * x + 3 * y),
    }.items():
        try:
            r = repr(f()).splitlines()[-1]
        except Exception as e:
            r = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        print(f"  {lab:18} -> {r}")
```

Output:

```
sparse=False
  c * (2*x + 3*y)    -> TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'LinearExpression' and 'LinearExpression'
  (2*x + 3*y) * c    -> +6 x + 9 y
  c * (2*x)          -> +6 x
  3 * (2*x + 3*y)    -> +6 x + 9 y
sparse=True
  c * (2*x + 3*y)    -> TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'LinearExpression' and 'LinearExpression'
  (2*x + 3*y) * c    -> +6 x + 9 y
  c * (2*x)          -> +6 x
  3 * (2*x + 3*y)    -> +6 x + 9 y
```

<details>
<summary>Traceback (without try/except)</summary>

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 18, in <module>
    c * (2 * x + 3 * y)
    ~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'LinearExpression' and 'LinearExpression'
```

</details>

The same asymmetry applies to non-constant one-term factors, e.g. `(x*0 + 3) * (2*x + 3*y)` raises while `(2*x + 3*y) * (x*0 + 3)` returns a `QuadraticExpression`.

### Expected Behavior

A constant expression acts like a scalar factor: `c * (2*x + 3*y)` returns the `LinearExpression` `+6 x + 9 y`, the same as `(2*x + 3*y) * c` and `3 * (2*x + 3*y)`.

@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+``gouraud`` shading supports data at quadrilaterals centers
+-----------------------------------------------------------
+
+`~.Axes.pcolormesh` previously required data at the corners of
+quadrilaterals for ``gouraud`` shading. It now also supports data
+defined at the centers of quadrilaterals.
+
+This now allows `~.Axes.pcolormesh` to provide both constant and
+linearly interpolated shading for each data location.
+
+=============== ======== =====================
+..              constant linearly interpolated
+=============== ======== =====================
+data at corners nearest  gouraud
+data at centers flat     gouraud
+=============== ======== =====================
+
+Shading can be switched for the same data location, allowing
+switches between ``nearest`` and ``gouraud``, and now also
+between ``flat`` and ``gouraud``.
+
+For example:
+
+.. plot::
+    :include-source: true
+    :alt: Switching between constant and linearly interpolated shading for data at corners and centers.
+
+    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+    import numpy as np
+
+    nrows, ncols = 3, 5
+    Z = np.arange(nrows * ncols).reshape(nrows, ncols)
+    x = np.arange(ncols + 1)
+    y = np.arange(nrows + 1)
+
+    fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, layout='constrained')

+    axs[0, 0].set_title('nearest: X, Y, Z same shape')

problem_statement.title: plt.pcolormesh shape mismatch when shading='gouraud'
problem_statement.body:
### Bug report

**Bug summary**

When running `plt.pcolormesh(X, Y, C, shading='flat')`, if `C.shape == (nrows, ncols)`, then if `X` and `Y` are 2-D arrays, their shapes must be either `(nrows, ncols)` or `(nrows+1, ncols+1)`.  If `shading='gouraud'`, however, the latter results in an error.  The code snippet below uses 1-D arrays for `X` and `Y`, but the same error occurs when they are the equivalent 2-D arrays.

**Code for reproduction**


```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
x = np.arange(-4, 5)
y = np.arange(-6, 7)
xe = np.linspace(-4.5, 4.5, 10)
ye = np.linspace(-6.5, 6.5, 14)
c = np.exp(-0.5*0.125*(x.reshape(1, -1)**2 + y.reshape(-1, 1)**2))
plt.pcolormesh(xe, ye, c, shading='flat')  # works
plt.pcolormesh(x, y, c, shading='gouraud')  # works
plt.pcolormesh(xe, ye, c, shading='gouraud')  # doesn't work
```

**Actual outcome**

```
Traceback (most recent call last):

  File "<ipython-input-67-154f761638cd>", line 1, in <module>
    plt.pcolormesh(xe, ye, c, shading='gouraud')

  File "/home/egranstedt/anaconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/matplotlib/pyplot.py", line 3245, in pcolormesh
    ret = ax.pcolormesh(*args, **kwargs)

  File "/home/egranstedt/anaconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/matplotlib/__init__.py", line 1892, in inner
    return func(ax, *args, **kwargs)

  File "/home/egranstedt/anaconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py", line 5569, in pcolormesh
    X, Y, C = self._pcolorargs('pcolormesh', *args, allmatch=allmatch)

  File "/home/egranstedt/anaconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/matplotlib/axes/_axes.py", line 5187, in _pcolorargs
    C.shape, Nx, Ny, funcname))

TypeError: Dimensions of C (13, 9) are incompatible with X (10) and/or Y (14); see help(pcolormesh)
```

**Expected outcome**

I expected `pcolormesh` would accept the same arrays for `X` and `Y  irrespective of the setting of the `shading` keyword argument.

**Matplotlib version**

- The error occurs with Matplotlib version 2.0.0 in the python 3.6 interpreter on Linux (installed via anaconda), but also seems to exist in older versions of Matplotlib (e.g., 1.5.1)

+def test_strict_filter_no_inplace_drop_deprecation_warning():
+    """Regression test for #2599.
+
+    ``strict="filter"`` must not trigger a ``DeprecationWarning`` from the
+    deprecated ``inplace`` parameter of ``pandas.DataFrame.drop`` (deprecated
+    in pandas 3). The non-inplace drop also guarantees the input frame is not
+    mutated unless validation is explicitly ``inplace``.

+    schema = DataFrameSchema(

+    df = pd.DataFrame({"keep": [1, 2], "other": [3, 4], "drop": [5, 6]})
+
+    with warnings.catch_warnings():
+        warnings.simplefilter("error", DeprecationWarning)
+        result = schema.validate(df)

+        result = schema.validate(df, inplace=True)

problem_statement.body: **Describe the bug** Pandas 3 is deprecating the `inplace` parameter of it's DataFrame methods. The method `drop` has already deprecated it. problem_statement.title: Point the generic HTTP 500 from a served Tesseract to debug mode
problem_statement.body:
When an endpoint raises, a served Tesseract responds with a bare `500 Internal Server Error`. Keeping tracebacks out of responses is deliberate, since exposing them would be unsafe in production. The traceback still goes to the server log, and debug mode (`tesseract serve --debug`, or `TESSERACT_DEBUG=1`) includes it in the response. The response mentions neither of these, though.

Feedback from hackathon participants suggests this costs real time. Unrelated bugs look identical from the client side, and people (and their coding agents) didn't find debug mode, even though the debugging guide documents it.

To reproduce:

```python
# tesseract_api.py
from pydantic import BaseModel

class InputSchema(BaseModel):
    x: float

class OutputSchema(BaseModel):
    y: float

def apply(inputs: InputSchema) -> OutputSchema:
    raise ValueError("boom")
```

```console
$ TESSERACT_API_PATH=tesseract_api.py tesseract-runtime serve --port 8000
$ curl -X POST localhost:8000/apply -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"inputs": {"x": 1}}'
Internal Server Error
```

Through the SDK, this surfaces as `RuntimeError: Error 500 from Tesseract: Internal Server Error`.

## Proposal

- **Runtime.** Outside debug mode, return a 500 whose body names the next step, for example: "Internal server error. The traceback is in the server log. Enable debug mode (`TESSERACT_DEBUG=1`, or `tesseract serve --debug`) to include it in responses." Leave debug mode unchanged. Since `serve.py` registers no handler for unhandled exceptions, the current body is the framework's default.
- **SDK.** When `_decode_response` gets a 500, add the same hint to the `RuntimeError`, so clients get it from runtimes that predate the change too (see #823).

## Open question

The right flag depends on how the Tesseract was started (`tesseract serve`, `tesseract-runtime serve`, `Tesseract.from_source`, a remote URL). One message that is correct for all of them probably has to name the environment variable and link the debugging guide, rather than spell out every variant.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_trial_argument_labels_1757.py
@@ -0,0 +1,255 @@
+"""A trial's arguments are labelled as the source names them (#1757).
+
+`vera test` labelled a trial's arguments in parameter order, counting each
+type from 0 left to right, so the first of two `@Nat` parameters was
+reported as `@Nat.0`, the name the source gives the second.  `@T.0` is the
+most recent binding of `T` (DE_BRUIJN.md), so a parameter's index counts
+the parameters of its type after it, and the first of two `@Nat`
+parameters is `@Nat.1`.  Three reports read the labels `_run_trials`
+writes: the text report's failing trials, the `--json` report's `args`,
+and the E703 description of a refuted proof.  A fourth reader,
+`_assume_on_arguments`, reads the values by position, so the labels change
+and the order of the arguments does not.
+
+The matrix holds the labels over parameter shapes (two of one type, three
+of one type, two types interleaved, a single parameter, a type once among
+others, an alias among its base type, a `String` pair through the raw ABI)
+by the three reports.  Each function's `requires` pins every
+parameter to a value of its own by the name the source gives it, so the
+tester's own generation puts that value at that parameter, and a report
+must show each value under the name that pinned it, in the parameters'
+order.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests import pipeline
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.matrix(decides=["vera/tester.py"])
+
+#: Each shape's parameters in order: the type, the name the source gives
+#: the parameter (its index counts the later parameters of its type), and
+#: the value its `requires` pins it to.
+SHAPES: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, str, int | bool | str], ...]] = {
+    "two of one type": (
+        ("Nat", "@Nat.1", 11), ("Nat", "@Nat.0", 12)),
+    "three of one type": (
+        ("Int", "@Int.2", -21), ("Int", "@Int.1", -22), ("Int", "@Int.0", -23)),
+    "two types interleaved": (
+        ("Int", "@Int.1", -31), ("Nat", "@Nat.1", 32),
+        ("Int", "@Int.0", -33), ("Nat", "@Nat.0", 34)),
+    "a single parameter": (
+        ("Int", "@Int.0", -41),),
+    "a type once among others": (
+        ("Int", "@Int.1", -51), ("Bool", "@Bool.0", True), ("Int", "@Int.0", -53)),
+    # A top-level alias is a slot type of its own (`naming.slot_name`): the
+    # checker binds `@Cnt` under `Cnt`, not under the `Nat` it resolves to.
+    "an alias among its base": (
+        ("Cnt", "@Cnt.1", 61), ("Nat", "@Nat.0", 62), ("Cnt", "@Cnt.0", 63)),
+    # `String` arguments reach the compiled function through the raw ABI
+    # (`execute`'s `raw_args`), and the E703 description quotes them.
+    "a `String` pair, through the raw ABI": (
+        ("String", "@String.1", "ab"), ("Int", "@Int.0", -71),
+        ("String", "@String.0", "cd")),
+}
+
+REPORTS = ("text", "json", "refutation")
+
+#: Every trial fails this `ensures`, which the verifier leaves to Tier 3, so
+#: every trial is reported with its arguments.  `Cnt` is the alias row's.
+_FAILING = """\
+type Cnt = Nat;
+
+public fn f({params} -> @Int)
+  requires({pins})
+  ensures(string_length(int_to_string(@Int.result)) == 99)
+  effects(pure)
+{{
+  0
+}}
+"""
+
+#: #1555's address comparison, which the verifier proves and every run
+#: refutes (E703); `{premise}` is a statement at the head of the body.  The
+#: instance is a checklist line of issue #1525: when that lands, the
+#: refutation cells and the premise repro need another refuted proof.
+_REFUTED = """\
+type Cnt = Nat;
+
+public fn f({params} -> @Int)
+  requires({pins})
+  ensures(@Int.result < 0)
+  effects(pure)
+{{
+{premise}  if mo(7) == mo(7) then {{ 0 - 1 }} else {{ 1 }}
+}}
+
+private fn mo(@Int -> @Option<Int>)
+  requires(true)
+  ensures(@Option<Int>.result == Some(@Int.0))
+  effects(pure)
+{{
+  match parse_int(show(@Int.0)) {{
+    Ok(@Int) -> Some(@Int.0),
+    Err(@String) -> Some(@Int.0)
+  }}
+}}
+"""
+
+
+def _shown(value: int | bool | str) -> int | str:
+    """A value as the text and `--json` reports show it: a `Bool` is the 1
+    or 0 the compiled function receives (`_extract_values`)."""
+    return value if isinstance(value, str) else int(value)
+
+
+def _rendered(value: int | bool | str) -> str:
+    """A value as the E703 description writes it (`_render_args`), a string
+    quoted."""
+    return json.dumps(value) if isinstance(value, str) else str(_shown(value))
+
+
+def _pin(name: str, value: int | bool | str) -> str:
+    if value is True:
+        return name
+    if value is False:
+        return f"!{name}"
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return f"{name} == {json.dumps(value)}"
+    return f"{name} == {value}"
+
+
+def _source(template: str, shape: tuple[tuple[str, str, int | bool | str], ...],
+            premise: str = "") -> str:
+    return template.format(
+        params=", ".join(f"@{ty}" for ty, _, _ in shape),
+        pins=" && ".join(_pin(name, value) for _, name, value in shape),
+        premise=premise)
+
+
+def _write(tmp_path: Path, source: str) -> Path:
+    path = tmp_path / "labels.vera"
+    path.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
+    return path
+
+
+def _text_trials(stdout: str) -> list[list[tuple[str, str]]]:
+    """Each failing trial's arguments as the text report prints them,
+    `    @T.n = v, ... -> message`."""
+    trials = []
+    for line in stdout.splitlines():
+        found = re.match(r"^    (@\S+ = .*?) -> ", line)
+        if found:
+            pairs = []
+            for pair in found.group(1).split(", "):
+                label, _, value = pair.partition(" = ")
+                pairs.append((label, value))
+            trials.append(pairs)
+    return trials
+
+
+def _refuted_trials(envelope: Any) -> list[str]:
+    """The arguments each E703 description names, `the trial on ... failed`."""
+    out = []
+    for diag in envelope["diagnostics"]:
+        if diag["error_code"] == "E703":
+            found = re.search(r"the trial on (.*?) failed", diag["description"])
+            assert found, diag["description"]
+            out.append(found.group(1))
+    return out
+
+
+def _reported(tmp_path: Path, report: str,
+              shape: tuple[tuple[str, str, int | bool | str], ...]) -> tuple[list[Any], Any]:
+    """What *report* shows for each failing trial of *shape*'s function, and
+    what it must show."""
+    if report == "text":
+        ran = pipeline.cli("test", "--trials", "3", _write(
+            tmp_path, _source(_FAILING, shape)))
+        assert ran.returncode != 0, ran.stdout
+        return _text_trials(ran.stdout), [
+            (name, str(_shown(value))) for _, name, value in shape]
+    if report == "json":
+        ran = pipeline.cli("test", "--json", "--trials", "3", _write(
+            tmp_path, _source(_FAILING, shape)))
+        [function] = ran.json()["functions"]
+        return [json.dumps(list(t["args"].items())) for t in function["failures"]], (
+            json.dumps([(name, _shown(value)) for _, name, value in shape]))
+    ran = pipeline.cli("test", "--json", "--distrust", "--trials", "3", _write(
+        tmp_path, _source(_REFUTED, shape)))
+    return _refuted_trials(ran.json()), ", ".join(
+        f"{name} = {_rendered(value)}" for _, name, value in shape)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("report", REPORTS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", SHAPES)
+def test_each_report_names_each_argument_as_the_source_does(
+        tmp_path: Path, shape: str, report: str) -> None:
+    """Every failing trial shows each pinned value under the name that pins
+    it, in the parameters' order."""
+    trials, expected = _reported(tmp_path, report, SHAPES[shape])
+    assert trials, f"{report} reported no failing trial"
+    for trial in trials:
+        assert trial == expected, (shape, report, trial)
+
+
+def test_the_names_are_de_bruijn_indices() -> None:
+    """The table states DE_BRUIJN.md's rule: a parameter of type `T` is
+    `@T.n`, *n* the number of later parameters of type `T`."""
+    for shape in SHAPES.values():
+        types = [ty for ty, _, _ in shape]
+        assert [name for _, name, _ in shape] == [
+            f"@{ty}.{types[k + 1:].count(ty)}" for k, ty in enumerate(types)]
+
+
+_REPRO = """\
+public fn pair(@Nat, @Nat -> @Int)
+  requires(@Nat.1 <= 0 && @Nat.0 >= 5 && @Nat.0 <= 9)
+  ensures(string_length(int_to_string(@Int.result)) == 99)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  0
+}
+"""
+
+
+def test_the_reported_program_repro(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    """#1757's program, its `requires` as the issue states it, failing
+    through a Tier 3 `ensures` rather than #1756's trap: the `requires`
+    bounds `@Nat.1`, the first parameter, to 0 and `@Nat.0`, the second,
+    to 5 to 9, and the report names them so."""
+    ran = pipeline.cli("test", "--json", "--distrust", "--trials", "5",
+                       _write(tmp_path, _REPRO))
+    [function] = ran.json()["functions"]
+    failures = function["failures"]
+    assert failures, function
+    for trial in failures:
+        args = trial["args"]
+        assert list(args) == ["@Nat.1", "@Nat.0"], args
+        assert args["@Nat.1"] == 0 and 5 <= args["@Nat.0"] <= 9, args
+
+
+def test_a_premise_reads_the_arguments_in_the_parameters_order_repro(
+        tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    """`_assume_on_arguments` evaluates an `assume` at the head of a refuted
+    function on the trial's values by position.  `@Nat.1 < @Nat.0` holds of
+    the pinned 11 and 12 in the parameters' order and fails of them
+    reversed, so the description says the arguments satisfy it."""
+    shape = SHAPES["two of one type"]
+    ran = pipeline.cli("test", "--json", "--distrust", "--trials", "3", _write(
+        tmp_path, _source(_REFUTED, shape,
+                          premise="  assume(@Nat.1 < @Nat.0);\n")))
+    descriptions = [
+        d["description"] for d in ran.json()["diagnostics"]
+        if d["error_code"] == "E703"]
+    assert descriptions, ran.stdout
+    for description in descriptions:
+        assert "the trial on @Nat.1 = 11, @Nat.0 = 12 failed" in description
+        assert "which these arguments satisfy" in description, description

problem_statement.title: [BUG] pandas pivot_longer: output aliases input under CoW
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

Bug in pandas `pivot_longer` (`janitor/functions/pivot.py`, dev @ `5b4e755`, pandas 3.0.6): the output shares memory with the input, so writes to the result modify the caller's DataFrame.

The performance half of this issue (the quadratic per-label `.value` loop) has moved to #1821.

### Bug

`_build_df` passes raw `ravel` views of the source blocks to `pd.DataFrame(..., copy=False)`. Copy-on-Write does not track those references:

```python
df2 = pd.DataFrame(np.arange(8.0).reshape(2, 4), columns=["x1", "x2", "x3", "x4"])
df2.insert(0, "id", [1, 2])
o2 = df2.pivot_longer(index="id", names_to=".value", names_pattern="(x)\\d")
o2.loc[0, "x"] = -1.0          # df2.loc[0, "x1"] is now -1.0
o3 = df2.pivot_longer(index="id")
o3.loc[0, "value"] = -7.0      # df2.loc[0, "x1"] is now -7.0
```

In a 2,000-case fuzz, in-place writes to the output changed the input in 405 cases, across the plain, `.value`-only (single and multiple labels), `.value` + other names, and `names_transform` paths.

Later review on #1820 found two more alias sources: `datetime64`/`timedelta64` value columns (`DatetimeArray`/`TimedeltaArray` ravel views), and `np.tile(DatetimeArray, 1)` for a datetime index column with a single value column.

## Fix

Copy only where a view of the input is created: after each `._values.ravel(...)` and after `np.tile` in `_build_index`, when `np.may_share_memory` reports overlap. Being fixed in #1820.

## Verification

- A regression test for each path: write to the output and assert the input is unchanged.
- The extra memory should be exactly one copy of the columns that were views. Nothing extra should be copied where pandas already returns new arrays.

Related: #1821, #1769 (polars).

problem_statement.title: find-updates: resolve via source_resolver when present
problem_statement.body:
Part of #1294 (Phase 8 of epic #1254). Branch: `new-resolver-config`.

## What needs to happen

Update `_find_newer_versions()` in `src/fromager/commands/find_updates.py`: it currently calls `overrides.find_and_invoke("get_resolver_provider", ...)` directly, so packages with `source:` config silently resolve through the legacy resolver. Use `sources.get_source_provider()` when `pbi.source_resolver` is present; fall back to the legacy path otherwise.

This is the one piece of #1294 with a live behavioral gap today.

## Tests

- `find-updates` for a new-config package resolves via the configured provider
- Legacy-config packages behave as before

## Notes

Independent of the other #1294 sub-issues; can be worked on in any order.

+class CognitoIdpOpenIdConfigurationResponse(BaseResponse):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(service_name="cognito-idp")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def serve_openid_configuration(*args) -> TYPE_RESPONSE:  # type: ignore

+        url = urlparse(args[1])

+        # The JWKS URI is relative to wherever this request was made, so that
+        # it can be reached in ServerMode as well.
+        issuer = f"https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{pool_id}"

+            "issuer": issuer,

+            "subject_types_supported": ["public"],
+            "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": ["RS256"],

problem_statement.title: `GET /<userPoolId>/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns 500 (Cognito IDP)
problem_statement.body:
moto's Cognito IDP backend serves `//.well-known/jwks.json` but not `//.well-known/openid-configuration`. `cognitoidp/urls.py` registers only the `jwks.json` path, so the discovery request matches no Cognito route and falls through to moto's generic host-based backend dispatch. That dispatch cannot find a service for the host and crashes with an `AttributeError`, which Werkzeug turns into an HTTP 500. Real Cognito user pools publish an OIDC discovery document at this path, and OIDC clients and resource servers (Spring Security `issuer-uri`, `oidc-client`, `authlib`, ...) fetch it before they ever look at `jwks_uri`. Anything that validates Cognito-issued tokens by discovery therefore cannot run against moto in server mode, even though the JWKS endpoint it would go on to use already works. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | moto | `5.2.1.dev0` (image `motoserver/moto:5.2.1`, created 2026-05-10) | | mode | ServerMode (`moto_server` / Docker image), no configuration | | Python | 3.13.13 | | Werkzeug | 3.1.8 | ## Reproduction ```bash docker run -d -p 5000:5000 motoserver/moto:5.2.1 # 1. create a user pool curl -s -X POST localhost:5000/ \ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1' \ -H 'X-Amz-Target: AWSCognitoIdentityProviderService.CreateUserPool' \ -H 'Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=test/20260101/us-east-1/cognito-idp/aws4_request, SignedHeaders=host, Signature=x' \ -d '{"PoolName":"barebones"}' # -> UserPool.Id = us-east-1_99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266 # 2. the registered well-known path works curl -i localhost:5000/us-east-1_99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266/.well-known/jwks.json # HTTP/1.1 200 OK # 3. the discovery document does not curl -i localhost:5000/us-east-1_99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266/.well-known/openid-configuration # HTTP/1.1 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR ``` ### Response ``` HTTP/1.1 500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR Server: Werkzeug/3.1.8 Python/3.13.13 Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 500 Internal Server Error

Internal Server Error

The server encountered an internal error and was unable to complete your request. ...

``` ### Server log ``` 172.17.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2026 19:30:58] "POST / HTTP/1.1" 200 - 172.17.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2026 19:30:58] "GET /us-east-1_99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266/.well-known/jwks.json HTTP/1.1" 200 - Unable to find appropriate backend for us-east-1.99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266.amazonaws.com.Remember to add the URL to urls.py, and run scripts/update_backend_index.py to index it. 172.17.0.1 - - [12/Oct/2026 19:30:58] "GET /us-east-1_99992fd7c57a42f5881e548d23407266/.well-known/openid-configuration HTTP/1.1" 500 - Error on request: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/werkzeug/serving.py", line 371, in run_wsgi execute(self.server.app) ~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/werkzeug/serving.py", line 332, in execute application_iter = app(environ, start_response) File "/moto/moto/moto_server/werkzeug_app.py", line 315, in __call__ backend_app = self.get_application(environ) File "/moto/moto/moto_server/werkzeug_app.py", line 236, in get_application app = self.create_app(backend) File "/moto/moto/moto_server/werkzeug_app.py", line 341, in create_backend_app backend_dict = backends.get_backend(service) File "/moto/moto/backends.py", line 828, in get_backend safe_name = name.replace("-", "") ^^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace' ``` ### Why it falls through `moto/cognitoidp/urls.py` as shipped: ```python from .responses import CognitoIdpJsonWebKeyResponse, CognitoIdpResponse url_bases = [r"https?://cognito-idp\.(.+)\.amazonaws.com"] url_paths = { "{0}/$": CognitoIdpResponse.dispatch, "{0}/(?P[^/]+)/.well-known/jwks.json$": CognitoIdpJsonWebKeyResponse.serve_json_web_key, } ``` There is no entry for `.well-known/openid-configuration`. ## Suggested fix 1. Register the route in `moto/cognitoidp/urls.py`, next to the existing `jwks.json` one: ```python "{0}/(?P[^/]+)/.well-known/openid-configuration$": CognitoIdpJsonWebKeyResponse.serve_openid_configuration, ``` 2. Add a handler to `CognitoIdpJsonWebKeyResponse` in `moto/cognitoidp/responses.py` that returns the discovery document as `application/json`: ```python @staticmethod def serve_openid_configuration(*args) -> TYPE_RESPONSE: # type: ignore full_url = args[1] parsed = urlparse(full_url) user_pool_id = parsed.path.strip("/").split("/")[0] region = user_pool_id.rsplit("_", 1)[0] if "_" in user_pool_id else "us-east-1" # Same function UserPool.create_jwt() uses for the "iss" claim, so a client that # compares a token's issuer with this document's issuer sees the same value, # including when MOTO_COGNITO_IDP_ISSUER_BASE_URL overrides the default host. issuer = issuer_url(region, user_pool_id) # Endpoint URLs come from the URL the request arrived on: in ServerMode that is # the only address reachable from the caller, and it is the one jwks.json # already relies on. base = f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc}/{user_pool_id}" config = { "issuer": issuer, "jwks_uri": f"{base}/.well-known/jwks.json", "token_endpoint": f"{base}/oauth2/token", "userinfo_endpoint": f"{base}/oauth2/userinfo", "subject_types_supported": ["public", "pairwise"], "grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code"], "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": ["RS256"], } return 200, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, json.dumps(config) ``` with `from urllib.parse import urlparse` and `from .utils import issuer_url` added to the imports. The `issuer_url` helper is already what token creation uses for `iss`; in the `5.2.1` tree that logic may still be inline, in which case this handler should call whatever `create_jwt` uses so the two stay identical. 3. Separate, smaller hardening (not required for the above): when no service matches a request, `get_application` passes `service=None` into `backends.get_backend`, which crashes on `name.replace(...)`. An unmatched URL should produce a clean 404 and not a 500 with a traceback. ## Proof that the fix works A build with the change above is published as `ghcr.io/starship-z/moto:cognito-oidc-discovery` (source: https://github.com/starship-z/moto, branch `cognito-oidc-discovery`). It is based on moto `5.2.4.dev0`. The same reproduction against it, run on 2026-10-12: ``` $ curl -i localhost:5000/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/.well-known/jwks.json HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json $ curl -i localhost:5000/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/.well-known/openid-configuration HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 561 {"issuer": "https://cognito-idp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed", "jwks_uri": "http://localhost:5000/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/.well-known/jwks.json", "token_endpoint": "http://localhost:5000/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/oauth2/token", "userinfo_endpoint": "http://localhost:5000/us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/oauth2/userinfo", "subject_types_supported": ["public", "pairwise"], "grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code"], "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": ["RS256"]} ``` Server log for the same run: ``` "POST / HTTP/1.1" 200 - "GET /us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/.well-known/jwks.json HTTP/1.1" 200 - "GET /us-east-1_6433ba30769441ef9d3bf64c8169d5ed/.well-known/openid-configuration HTTP/1.1" 200 - ``` The `urls.py` in that image differs from stock only by the added `openid-configuration` route. Happy for the maintainers to implement this themselves from the description above. The branch linked in the proof section can also become available as a PR if that is easier to review.

--- a/tests/unit/test_regressions.py

@@ -2788,3 +2788,65 @@ def test_lines_before_imports_keeps_import_after_indented_block() -> None:

+def test_indented_imports_followed_by_less_indented_import_issue_2010() -> None:
+    """Imports in an indented block that is directly followed by a less indented import
+    must still be sorted as an indented section.
+    See: https://github.com/PyCQA/isort/issues/2010
+    """
+    code = (
+        "import sys\n"
+        "\n"
+        "if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):\n"
+        "    from typing import LiteralString, Never\n"
+        "else:\n"
+        "    from typing_extensions import LiteralString\n"
+        "    from typing_extensions import Never\n"
+        "\n"
+        "import third_party_library\n"
+    )
+    expected = (
+        "import sys\n"
+        "\n"
+        "if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):\n"
+        "    from typing import LiteralString, Never\n"
+        "else:\n"
+        "    from typing_extensions import LiteralString, Never\n"
+        "\n"
+        "import third_party_library\n"
+    )
+    assert isort.code(code) == expected
+    assert isort.code(expected) == expected
+
+    # The same block, sorted the same way as when code follows it.
+    code = "def f():\n    import os\n    import a\n    import os\nimport b\n"
+    expected = "def f():\n    import os\n\n    import a\n\nimport b\n"
+    assert isort.code(code) == expected
+    assert isort.code(expected) == expected
+    assert isort.code(code, lines_before_imports=1) == expected
+
+    code = "class C:\n    def f(self):\n        import a\n\n    import b\n"
+    expected = "class C:\n    def f(self):\n        import a\n\n    import b\n"
+    assert isort.code(code) == expected
+    assert isort.code(expected) == expected
+
+    # A dedent of one level out of two, again sorted as when code follows it.
+    code = (
+        "class C:\n"
+        "    def f(self):\n"
+        "        import b\n"
+        "        import a\n"
+        "    import d\n"
+        "    import c\n"
+    )
+    expected = (
+        "class C:\n"
+        "    def f(self):\n"
+        "        import a\n"
+        "        import b\n"
+        "    import c\n"
+        "    import d\n"
+    )
+    assert isort.code(code) == expected
+    assert isort.code(expected) == expected

problem_statement.title: Formatting problems in an  `else` conditional import
problem_statement.body:
Given the following code in a `.pyi` file

```python
import sys
import weakref
from typing import Any, ClassVar, overload, type_check_only

if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    from typing import LiteralString, Never
else:
    from typing_extensions import LiteralString
    from typing_extensions import Never
```

`isort` automatically formats it to 

```python
import sys
import weakref
from typing import Any, ClassVar, overload, type_check_only


if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    from typing import LiteralString, Never
else:
    from typing_extensions import LiteralString, Never  # <<< `isort`ed line
```

which is expected.

---

However, if you add additional imports below the conditional in the first example,

```python
import sys
import weakref
from typing import Any, ClassVar, overload, type_check_only

if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    from typing import LiteralString, Never
else:
    from typing_extensions import LiteralString
    from typing_extensions import Never

import third_party_library  # <<< Additional import
```

`isort` no longer formats the `else` conditional imports:

```python
import sys
import weakref
from typing import Any, ClassVar, overload, type_check_only


if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    from typing import LiteralString, Never
else:
    from typing_extensions import LiteralString  # <<< Not formatted
    from typing_extensions import Never          # <<< Not formatted

import third_party_library  # <<< Additional import
```

---

**isort version: 5.10.1**

**isort configuration**:

> [settings]
lines_before_imports=1
lines_after_imports=2
extra_standard_library=typing_extensions
profile=black
multi_line_output=3
combine_as_imports=True

title: fix(polars): exclude explicit columns from regex alias selectors (#2343)
issue_title: Make `alias` selector in `Field` mutually exclusive with the non-`alias` fields.

 """Validation backend for polars DataFrameSchema."""
 
 import copy
+import re
 import traceback
 import warnings
 from collections.abc import Callable
@@ -32,6 +33,11 @@ def _to_lazy(df: PolarsFrame) -> pl.LazyFrame:
         return df
 
 
+def get_lazyframe_column_names(df: PolarsFrame) -> list[str]:
+    """Return the column names of a polars DataFrame or LazyFrame."""
+    return df.collect_schema().names()
+
+
 def _to_frame_kind(lf: pl.LazyFrame, kind: type[PolarsFrame]) -> PolarsFrame:
     if issubclass(kind, pl.DataFrame):
         return lf.collect()
@@ -301,6 +307,13 @@ def collect_schema_components(
                 columns[col_name] = Column(schema.dtype, name=str(col_name))
 
         schema_components = []
+        # Names of explicit (non-regex) columns in this schema. A regex
+        # ``alias=...`` field must not also govern these columns (issue #2343).
+        explicit_column_names = {
+            name
+            for name, c in columns.items()
+            if not getattr(c, "regex", False)
+        }
         for col_name, col in columns.items():
             if (
                 col.required  # type: ignore
@@ -318,6 +331,51 @@ def collect_schema_components(
                 # disable coercion at the schema component level since the
                 # dataframe-level schema already coerced it.
                 col.coerce = False  # type: ignore
+                # If this component is a regex selector that would also match
+                # any explicit (non-regex) column, expand it into one
+                # non-regex component per non-explicit match so explicit
+                # columns are left to their own schema (issue #2343).
+                if getattr(col, "regex", False) and explicit_column_names:
+                    all_matched_names = [
+                        name
+                        for name in get_lazyframe_column_names(check_obj)
+                        if re.fullmatch(col.name or "", name)
+                    ]
+                    matched_names = [
+                        name
+                        for name in all_matched_names
+                        if name not in explicit_column_names
+                    ]
+                    if matched_names:
+                        col.regex = False
+                        col.name = matched_names[0]
+                        for extra_name in matched_names[1:]:
+                            extra = copy.deepcopy(col)
+                            extra.name = extra_name
+                            schema_components.append(extra)
+                    elif all_matched_names:

+                        # nothing left for this component to govern. Mirror
+                        # the required/optional no-match semantics of the
+                        # component path.

+                                message=(
+                                    f"Column regex name='{col.name}' did not "
+                                    "match any non-explicit columns in the "
+                                    "dataframe."
+                                ),
+                                failure_cases=get_lazyframe_column_names(
+                                    check_obj
+                                ),
+                                check=f"no_regex_column_match('{col.name}')",
+                                reason_code=(
+                                    SchemaErrorReason.INVALID_COLUMN_NAME
+                                ),
+                            )
+                        continue
                 schema_components.append(col)
 
         return schema_components
@@ -507,6 +565,14 @@ def _coerce_dtype_helper(

+        # Names of explicit (non-regex) columns in this schema. A regex

diff --git a/tests/polars/test_polars_model.py b/tests/polars/test_polars_model.py
index 811161026..a0083a4cb 100644
--- a/tests/polars/test_polars_model.py
+++ b/tests/polars/test_polars_model.py
@@ -577,6 +577,82 @@ class Schema(DataFrameModel):
     assert exc_info.value.failure_cases["failure_case"].to_list() == ["z"]
 
 
+@pytest.mark.xfail(
+    condition=CONFIG.use_narwhals_backend,
+    reason="Narwhals backend does not exclude explicit columns from regex "
+    "aliases (issue #2343)",
+    strict=True,
+)
+def test_alias_regex_does_not_override_explicit_column_dtype() -> None:
+    """Issue #2343 regression test.
+
+    When a model declares an explicit column alongside a regex ``alias=...``
+    field, the alias must not coerce the explicit column to its own dtype.
+    """
+    from pandera.typing.polars import Series
+
+    class Model(DataFrameModel):
+        class Config:
+            coerce = True
+
+        index_column: Series[int]
+        anything_else: Series[str] = Field(alias=r".*", regex=True)
+
+    df = pl.DataFrame(
+        {
+            "index_column": [1.0],
+            "this_must_become_string": [1.0],
+        }
+    )
+
+    out = Model.validate(df)
+    assert out.schema["index_column"] == pl.Int64
+    assert out.schema["this_must_become_string"] == pl.String
+
+    # A frame containing only the explicit column must not let the alias
+    # govern it: the required alias raises its own no-match error instead
+    # of validating index_column against the alias dtype.
+    with pytest.raises(SchemaError, match="did not match any non-explicit"):
+        Model.validate(pl.DataFrame({"index_column": [1.0]}))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.xfail(
+    condition=CONFIG.use_narwhals_backend,
+    reason="Narwhals backend does not exclude explicit columns from regex "
+    "aliases (issue #2343)",
+    strict=True,
+)
+def test_alias_regex_still_coerces_dynamic_unmatched_columns() -> None:
+    """Issue #2343 companion test.
+
+    A regex ``alias=...`` must still govern columns that are not declared
+    explicitly in the model, even when the alias's regex is broad enough to
+    also match explicit columns.
+    """
+    from pandera.typing.polars import Series
+
+    class Model(DataFrameModel):
+        class Config:
+            coerce = True
+
+        index_column: Series[int]
+        anything_else: Series[str] = Field(alias=r".*", regex=True)
+
+    # Lazy variant: exercises the same fix on the lazy validation path.
+    df = pl.LazyFrame(
+        {
+            "index_column": [1.0],
+            "this_must_become_string": [1.0],
+        }
+    )
+
+    out = Model.validate(df).collect()
+    # The unmatched column must be coerced to String by the alias path.
+    assert out.schema["this_must_become_string"] == pl.String
+    # And the explicit column must keep its declared Int64 dtype.
+    assert out.schema["index_column"] == pl.Int64
+
+

problem_statement.title: Make `alias` selector in `Field` mutually exclusive with the non-`alias` fields.
problem_statement.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I work with matrices where, except for a few indices, the majority of column names are not predefined. I would still like to validate and coerce them using pandera. 

I hoped that this would work:
```python
import pandera.polars as pa
import polars as pl
from pandera.api.polars.model_config import BaseConfig
from pandera.typing import Series


class Model(pa.DataFrameModel):
    class Config(BaseConfig):  # noqa: D106
        coerce=True
    index_column: Series[int]
    anything_else: Series[str] = pa.Field(alias=r".*", regex=True)


df = pl.LazyFrame({
    "index_column": [1.0],
    "this_must_become_string": [1.0]
})

Model(df).collect()
```

Expected_output:
```bash
shape: (1, 2)
┌──────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│ index_column ┆ this_must_become_string │
│ ---          ┆ ---                     │
│ i64          ┆ str                     │
╞══════════════╪═════════════════════════╡
│ 1            ┆ 1.0                     │
└──────────────┴─────────────────────────┘
```

Real output:
```bash
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\dataframe\model.py", line 246, in __new__
    return cast(DataFrameBase[Self], cls.validate(*args, **kwargs))
                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\polars\model.py", line 153, in validate
    result = cls.to_schema().validate(
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\polars\container.py", line 57, in validate
    output = self.get_backend(check_obj).validate(
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\backends\polars\container.py", line 139, in validate
    error_handler.collect_error(
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\base\error_handler.py", line 98, in collect_error
    raise schema_error from original_exc
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\backends\polars\container.py", line 210, in run_schema_component_checks
    result = schema_component.validate(check_obj, lazy=lazy)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\polars\components.py", line 153, in validate
    output = self.get_backend(check_obj).validate(
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\backends\polars\components.py", line 123, in validate
    error_handler = self.run_checks_and_handle_errors(
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\backends\polars\components.py", line 193, in run_checks_and_handle_errors
    error_handler.collect_error(
  File "<shortened>.venv\Lib\site-packages\pandera\api\base\error_handler.py", line 98, in collect_error
    raise schema_error from original_exc
pandera.errors.SchemaError: expected column 'index_column' to have type Int64, got String
```

Apparently, the float value in `index_column` column has been converted to a String before running the validation to convert it into integer. I only want `index_column` to be coerced to an int in this case.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to define alias in Field such that it is mutually exclusive with the non-alias columns.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I tried to solve this using negative lookahead regex (`pa.Field(alias=r'(?!index_column$).*'`, regex=True), but that isn't supported by polars' regex engine.

**Additional context**
Pandera has been a very helpful tool, thanks for the great work!!

problem_statement.title: Investigate increasing `RUNLIMIT` for Everest
problem_statement.body:
Everest runs can exceed the maximum  RUNLIMIT  set on LSF, and the jobs are terminated before they complete. Ert and Everest currently share the same limit, which is too low for long-running Everest jobs.

We should look into the following:
• Can we make the  RUNLIMIT  configurable?
• Would it be better if we apply a higher  RUNLIMIT  automatically to Everest-jobs? 


The proposed temp-fix is to use `bmod` to increase the `RUNLIMIT`

Issue reported on [Slack](https://equinor.slack.com/archives/CGAFAQLTE/p1791464129193959)

problem_statement.title: Genelic type statement is not supported
problem_statement.body:
The following code works:

```python
from serde import serde

type Point = tuple[float, float]
type Polygon = tuple[Point, ...]


@serde
class Figure:
    name: str
    polygon: Polygon


def main() -> None:
    fig = Figure("test", ((0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.73), (-1.0, 1.73)))
    print(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

However, the following code, which is essentially the same, does not work:

```python
from serde import serde

type Point[T] = tuple[T, T]
type Polygon[T] = tuple[Point[T], ...]


@serde
class Figure:
    name: str
    polygon: Polygon[float]


def main() -> None:
    fig = Figure("test", ((0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.73), (-1.0, 1.73)))
    print(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
serde.compat.SerdeError: Unsupported type: Polygon
```

If we write the same code using the older syntax that does not use the `type` statement, it will work correctly:

```python
from typing import TypeAlias, TypeVar

from serde import serde

T = TypeVar("T")

Point: TypeAlias = tuple[T, T]
Polygon: TypeAlias = tuple[Point[T], ...]


@serde
class Figure:
    name: str
    polygon: Polygon[float]


def main() -> None:
    fig = Figure("test", ((0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 1.73), (-1.0, 1.73)))
    print(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

---

The environment is as follows:

OS: Windows 11
Python: 3.14.7 on uv
pyserde: 0.33.1
beartype: 0.22.9

problem_statement.title: robots.txt enforcement fails OPEN for 2nd+ concurrent same-host request (RobotsTxtMiddleware + Twisted Deferred.asFuture())
problem_statement.body:
## What happened

With `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, a path disallowed by robots.txt was fetched (HTTP 200) instead of being blocked — but only when it was the **2nd or later concurrent request to the same host**. Reproduced 4/4 runs, deterministically.

**Versions:** Scrapy 2.19, Python 3.12 (Twisted as bundled with the Scrapy 2.19 install — exact version available on request).

## Reproduction

1. Serve a local test site (`python -m http.server`) with robots.txt containing:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /private/
```
2. Run a spider with `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, `DOWNLOAD_DELAY=1.0`, `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1`, AutoThrottle enabled, honest User-Agent, requesting three URLs on that host: a live page, a 404, and `/private/x.html`.
3. Observe: `/private/x.html` returns 200 and reaches the parse callback instead of being filtered by the robots middleware.

## Root cause (instrumented)

Concurrent same-host requests share a single Twisted `Deferred` for the robots.txt fetch/parse inside `RobotsTxtMiddleware`. The middleware converts that Deferred per-waiter via `Deferred.asFuture()` — and Twisted's `asFuture()` delivers the real result to the **first** future and **`None`** to the second. The second waiter therefore gets `parser=None`, and `process_request_2` treats `None` as "no parser available → allow the request."

So robots.txt enforcement **silently fails open** for every concurrent same-host request after the first, on the very first robots.txt fetch for a host.

## Expected behavior

All waiters on the shared robots.txt Deferred should receive the parsed result (or all should fail closed — block the request — if the parse result is unavailable).

## Suggested fix directions

- Share the *parsed* result (not the raw Deferred) across waiters; or
- Fail closed: treat `parser=None` as "deny" rather than "allow" in `process_request_2`.

## Workaround

Serialize same-host requests so two requests never race the first robots.txt fetch of a host (e.g. `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN=1` plus a per-host delay), or pre-fetch robots.txt before crawling.

## Why this matters

Fail-open robots.txt enforcement is a compliance footgun: users who set `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True` believe disallowed paths are never fetched. Under concurrency, that guarantee silently breaks.

---
*Found while building a polite liveness-checker that deliberately serializes per-host requests; the serialization accidentally immunized us, which is how the race was isolated. Happy to provide the minimal spider + test server scripts.*

problem_statement.title: gfql: rows(table=nodes, source=alias) multiplies rows for duplicate node ids and joins null ids to each other
problem_statement.body:
Found while pinning the seeded node-lookup fast path (parity harness on the branch for the seeded fast paths, 2026-09-04).

1. Duplicate node ids: with two node rows carrying `id = 7`, `MATCH (p {id: 7}) RETURN p.age AS a` on the full path returns 8 rows on pandas and cuDF (2 duplicate rows → 2^3 through the chain's forward/reverse/combine self-joins); polars returns 2. The expected answer is one row per matching node row (2).
2. Null ids: with two rows whose `id` is null, `MATCH (p {name: 'n3'}) RETURN p.id, p.age` returns both null-id rows on the full path (NaN-keyed merge matches NaN to NaN) instead of the one row that matches the predicate. A seeded typed hop whose seed row has a null id raises `GFQLTypeError` on the full path (merge object vs float64) instead of returning no rows.

The seeded fast paths (`_execute_seeded_node_lookup_fast_path`, `_execute_seeded_typed_hop_fast_path`) return the intended answer for these inputs; `graphistry/tests/compute/gfql/test_seeded_node_lookup_fastpath.py::test_node_lookup_returns_each_duplicate_id_row_once` pins the fast answer on all three engines. The full path should agree; until it does, the differential parity tests exclude duplicate and null ids.

Where: `graphistry/compute/chain.py` `_chain_impl` combine step (self-join on the node id) and `graphistry/compute/gfql/row/frame_ops.py` `rows(source=...)`; the merges should key on row position for node-frame lookups, and null ids must never link.

problem_statement.title: Groupby rle_id is slow and ignores the caller's grouping
problem_statement.body:
Groupby `rle_id` computes IDs with `df.groupby(grp.keys).apply(_compute_rle)`, i.e. a Python function per group on a freshly rebuilt groupby. On `dev` (`9df51bc7`) this is slow and gives wrong results or errors for several groupings.

## Performance

Calling a Python function per group scales with the number of groups. For example, 1M rows / ~630k groups takes ~172 s.

## Correctness

Regrouping from `grp.keys` ignores how the caller grouped:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({"k": [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2], "v": [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3]})

# level= grouping is ignored (grp.keys is None), IDs don't restart per group
df.set_index("k").groupby(level=0).rle_id("v").obj["rle_id"].tolist()
# [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3]; expected [1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1]

# dropna=False is ignored: rows with missing keys get NaN instead of their own group
pd.DataFrame({"k": [1.0, np.nan, 1.0, np.nan], "v": [1, 1, 2, 2]}).groupby("k", dropna=False).rle_id("v")

# duplicate index labels: IDs are aligned by label and land on the wrong rows
pd.DataFrame({"k": [1, 2, 1, 2, 1], "v": [1, 1, 2, 1, 2]}, index=[0, 0, 1, 1, 0]).groupby("k").rle_id("v")

# multiple keys with equally sized groups: apply returns a DataFrame, the stack path raises
pd.DataFrame({"k": [1.0], "k2": [0], "v": [2.0]}).groupby(["k", "k2"]).rle_id("v")
# TypeError: incompatible index of inserted column with frame index
```

On a random grid of 960 groupings (NaN values/keys, categorical keys, 1-2 keys, 1-2 columns, `sort`/`dropna`/`observed`, duplicate index), the current implementation raises in 184 cases and gives wrong IDs in 29.

## Proposal

Vectorise the change detection: compute the previous value in each group with a grouped `shift`, flag the first row of each group with `cumcount() == 0`, then take a grouped `cumsum` of the flags. Use the groupby's own grouper (`grp._grouper`, already used in `expand_grid`/`pivot`) instead of regrouping from `grp.keys`.

Found while benchmarking #1826.

problem_statement.title: skip_gitignore=true will break ignoring directories defined in skip during filesystem traversal
problem_statement.body:
### Description
When starting isort with `--skip_gitignore`, directories that should not be traversed because they are configured in `skip` will be traversed.

From what I've seen, this is purely a performance problem, so all files that should be skipped will be filtered out at some later point.

### Instructions to reproduce
Minimal setup (note: "node_modules" is in the default skip values.)
```bash
# assuming isort 5.10.1 is installed (`pip3 install isort`)
mkdir test && cd test
git init
mkdir -p node_modules/this_should_not_be_accessed
touch test.py
strace isort . 2>&1 | grep this_should_not  # as expected, not queried
strace isort --skip-gitignore . 2>&1 | grep this_should_not  # suddenly, stat and open syscalls appear
```

On a side note: Add more files, and the node_modules folder will be queried more often:

```bash
touch test2.py
strace isort --skip-gitignore . 2>&1 | grep this_should_not  # 2 stat and 2 open calls
touch test3.py
strace isort --skip-gitignore . 2>&1 | grep this_should_not  # 3 stat and 3 open calls
```

adding `node_modules` to a `.gitignore` doesn't help, even though the directory should then be double-ignored by isort (this is #1895).
```bash
echo "node_modules" >> .gitignore
strace isort --skip-gitignore . 2>&1 | grep this_should_not  # 3 stat and 3 open calls
```

### Environment & Versions
Run on ubuntu21.10 with python3.9.7. Actual syscalls probably depend on the python interpreter, if you can't reproduce, I'll probably be able to figure out what python code causes the access.


### Related Issues
Closely related to #1895, but if I undestand that issue correctly, it does not talk about `skip` at all, but just files from .gitignore. ~It seems to me that the current PR for #1895, #1900, would fix this.~
Possibly related #1762 and #1777, both read as if they were fixed.

### Background
Yesterday, I realized that `isort` takes >90 seconds to run on one project where it processes 107 files with approximately 10k lines of code. Turns out, it doesn't need 90 seconds to process, but rather 89s to traverse what feels like the entire file system, only to then do its actual work in ~1s:
```bash
time isort --show-files . > isort_output.txt
real  1m35.831s

time cat isort_files.txt | xargs isort
real 0m0.896s
```
which is absurd, considering that `black` also finds the code files and finishes in 3 seconds. I wasn't able to get `isort` to skip reading directories it really doesn't need to access (venv, node_modules, web server static files, ...)

problem_statement.title: redact_secrets masks the detail after an exception class name (KeyError: '[REDACTED]')
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

`redact_secrets` (`pipecat/utils/security/redaction.py`, shipped in 1.13.0) masks the value of a `Name: detail` pair when the NAME contains a credential word, and an exception class name often does: `KeyError` holds `key`, `InvalidTokenError` holds `token`, `ExpiredSignatureError` holds `signature`.
So the text an `ErrorFrame` (or any string passed through it) carries for such an exception loses its detail: `KeyError: '[REDACTED]'`.

## Repro (pipecat-ai 1.13.0)

```python
from pipecat.utils.security.redaction import redact_secrets

for text in (
    "KeyError: 'audio_content'",
    "InvalidTokenError: signature has expired",
    "ExpiredSignatureError: Signature has expired",
    "TokenExpiredError: jwt expired",
):
    print(repr(text), "->", repr(redact_secrets(text)))
```

Output:

```
"KeyError: 'audio_content'" -> "KeyError: '[REDACTED]'"
'InvalidTokenError: signature has expired' -> 'InvalidTokenError: [REDACTED] has expired'
'ExpiredSignatureError: Signature has expired' -> 'ExpiredSignatureError: [REDACTED] has expired'
'TokenExpiredError: jwt expired' -> 'TokenExpiredError: [REDACTED] expired'
```

## Why it matters

`ErrorFrame.__post_init__` masks `error` with `redact_secrets`, and services build that text from the exception (`llm_service.py` formats `f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"`, and many services use `f"...{e}"`).
A message that starts with the class name is the shape that loses its detail, so the frame, the log line and the RTVI message all lose the one fact that says what failed (the missing dict key, the reason a token was refused), with nothing in the output to say the text was masked.

## Proposal

A name whose last word is `error`, `exception` or `warning` is not a credential name; the credential words stay as they are.
In `_is_credential_name`, before the `return`:

```python
    # An exception or warning name (KeyError, InvalidTokenError) names what went wrong,
    # not a credential; the text after it is the explanation.
    if parts and parts[-1] in {"error", "exception", "warning"}:
        return False
```

With that guard the four examples above print unchanged, and the credential cases still mask:

```
'api_key: abc123'              -> 'api_key: [REDACTED]'
'X-Api-Key: abc123'            -> 'X-Api-Key: [REDACTED]'
'Authorization: Bearer abc123' -> 'Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]'
'token=abc123'                 -> 'token=[REDACTED]'
'password: hunter2'            -> 'password: [REDACTED]'
```

Limits, for the record:
- A name that does not end in one of the three words (`SignatureDoesNotMatch: ...`) still masks.
- A credential field that really ends in `error` (`token_error`) would stop being masked; its value is an error description, not a secret.
- An alternative with the same effect for the common shape: skip a `Name:` whose name is a CamelCase identifier ending in `Error` or `Exception`. The last-word rule is the smaller change and also covers snake_case and kebab-case names.

Happy to send a PR if the rule is agreeable.

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: v0.3 JSON-RPC compat adapter returns -32603 for all A2A errors (e.g. TaskNotFound should be -32001)
problem_statement.body:
### What happened?

With `create_jsonrpc_routes(..., enable_v0_3_compat=True)`, A2A errors raised while handling v0.3 JSON-RPC requests are returned as `-32603 Internal error` instead of their A2A error codes. The v1.0 dispatcher maps them correctly.

| Request | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| v1.0 `GetTask`, unknown id | `-32001` | `-32001` |
| v0.3 `tasks/get`, unknown id | `-32001` | `-32603` |
| v0.3 `tasks/cancel`, unknown id | `-32001` | `-32603` |
| v0.3 `message/send` with unknown `taskId` | `-32001` | `-32603` |
| v0.3 `tasks/resubscribe`, streaming not supported | `-32004` | `-32603` |

A v0.3 client therefore cannot distinguish "task not found" from a server failure; the SDK's own v0.3 `JsonRpcTransport` maps the code back to `InternalError` instead of `TaskNotFoundError`.

**Cause:** in `src/a2a/compat/v0_3/jsonrpc_adapter.py`, `A2AError`s from the request handler fall through to the generic `except Exception` in `handle_request` (and in the streaming `event_generator`), which wraps them in `InternalError`. `JsonRpcDispatcher` handles `A2AError` explicitly, and the v0.3 gRPC handler maps them via `_ERROR_CODE_MAP`.

**Reproduction** (main @ 261c074, also 1.2.2):

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.testclient import TestClient

from a2a.server.agent_execution import AgentExecutor
from a2a.server.request_handlers import DefaultRequestHandler
from a2a.server.routes import create_jsonrpc_routes
from a2a.server.tasks import InMemoryTaskStore
from a2a.types import AgentCapabilities, AgentCard


class NoopExecutor(AgentExecutor):
    async def execute(self, context, event_queue): ...
    async def cancel(self, context, event_queue): ...


card = AgentCard(name='t', description='t', version='1', capabilities=AgentCapabilities())
handler = DefaultRequestHandler(agent_executor=NoopExecutor(), task_store=InMemoryTaskStore(), agent_card=card)
app = Starlette(routes=create_jsonrpc_routes(request_handler=handler, rpc_url='/', enable_v0_3_compat=True))
client = TestClient(app)


def call(method, params, version):
    body = {'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': '1', 'method': method, 'params': params}
    return client.post('/', json=body, headers={'A2A-Version': version}).json()['error']['code']


print(call('GetTask', {'id': 'missing'}, '1.0'))    # -32001
print(call('tasks/get', {'id': 'missing'}, '0.3'))  # -32603, expected -32001
```

**Expected:** A2A errors keep their JSON-RPC codes on the v0.3 path. Errors that only exist in v1.0 (e.g. `-32009` VersionNotSupported) should stay `-32603`, since v0.3 clients don't know those codes.

I have a fix with tests ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Relevant log output

```shell
-32001
   -32603
```

problem_statement.title: Minos confidence fit not reporting failure in FluxPoint upper-limit
problem_statement.body: As discussed in the dev call/gammapyv2 paper call of Sept 25th, there are some strange behaviour of the reported upper limit computed when using `FluxPointEstimator`. The devil is in the details and here is what we understood so far. So when simulating a SpectrumDatasetONOFF with no source signal (pure bkg), we compute UL via the `FluxPointEstimator` and compare it to what you get with the `stat_scan`. In theory the 95% UL is when the LL increases by 3.84 (1 dof) and the LL profile UL should match the blue curve and the horizontal dotted line in the plot below. While this is true in most cases, it happens that the LL profile UL is not at all at that intersection even when the LL profile looks "normal". This is due to the fact that internally, we rely on the Confidence function from Minos which uses brentq and does not rely on the computed `stat_scan`. A possible explanation is that Minos confidence failed and did not report it as the `success` attribute is `True` in this case but this related to the Fit results and not the Minos Confidence success. So we need to investigate if Minos Confidence failed here and find a way to report it. The other issue is that via the Confidence Minos function, it ignores the min,max values set on the parameter (the reported UL can be negative when min was set to zero). It also ignores (wihtout telling you) the attribute `estimator.norm.scan_min` which is confusing for the user. So we probably to understand this better, at the minimum any failure should be propagated back to the high level object to filter unsuccessful events.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", ["ansi", "sqlite"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "sql,expected",

+        ("SELECT\n17\n-- comment\n;SELECT 29;", [[(17,)], [(29,)]]),
+        (
